items.title: FG targets stronger local capacity for energy security
items.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Federal Government has expressed its readiness to strengthen local industrial capacity, infrastructure and investment as part of efforts to achieve energy security and accelerate Nigeria’s economic transformation. The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, said energy security went beyond the availability of natural resources to include the capacity to produce, process, transport and distribute energy reliably and affordably for the benefit of citizens. Akume spoke in Port Harcourt at the 10th Africa Energy Summit, organised by the Solewant Energy Training Institute, a subsidiary of Solewant Group, with the theme, “Scaling Innovative Industrial Capacity for Africa’s Energy Security.” Represented by his Special Assistant on Technical Matters, Prof. Babatunde Benerd, the SGF said Nigeria’s ambition for economic growth, industrialisation and job creation depended on an energy system capable of meeting the needs of households, businesses and industries. He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu considered reforms in the energy sector, investment and industrial development critical to the country’s economic transformation. “The current administration is pursuing reforms aimed at improving the investment climate, strengthening domestic production and creating conditions for productive activities,” he said. Akume said the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act had provided a framework for improved governance, clearer institutional responsibilities and increased investment across the oil and gas value chain. He added that the government was promoting domestic gas utilisation, compressed natural gas development, investment in energy infrastructure and reforms in the electricity sector. The SGF stressed that local content should go beyond Nigerian participation in petroleum projects to building competitive enterprises capable of manufacturing products, providing specialised services, creating jobs and competing internationally. Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the President on Energy, Olu Verheijen, represented by Dr Olusegun Amoda, said recent reforms in the sector had helped restore investor confidence and attract fresh investments. Verheijen said the administration had introduced executive orders and policy directives to provide fiscal incentives for investors, reduce contracting timelines and costs, and strengthen local content in the petroleum industry. She said the reforms had contributed to investment decisions worth more than $8 billion in oil and gas projects, adding that improved regulatory stability and security in the Niger Delta had helped create a more favourable investment climate. According to her, oil and gas projects require fabrication, engineering, drilling services, equipment, logistics and maintenance, creating opportunities for local businesses across the value chain. She, however, cautioned against treating local content as protection from competition, saying it should instead be used to develop Nigerian companies capable of competing globally on cost, quality and reliability. Verheijen said energy security also depended on skilled manpower, urging stakeholders to invest in training welders, inspectors, process safety engineers, project managers and other technical professionals. Earlier, the Group Chief Executive Officer of Solewant Group, Solomon Ewanehi, said Africa must move beyond discussions about its natural resources to making deliberate investments that would translate its resource wealth into industrial growth and prosperity. He said the summit, which had served as a platform for ideas over the past decade, should increasingly become a forum for decisions, partnerships and practical solutions to the continent’s energy challenges. Ewanehi said Africa had enormous energy resources, including oil, gas, wind and hydro, as well as human capital, but noted that the availability of resources alone could not guarantee prosperity. He linked industrial development to a change in mindset, citing his books, Unlocking Africa’s Energy Future: Strategies to Sustainable Growth and Development and The Power of Mindset Transformation for Success, which he said highlighted the connection between individual growth and continental development. He said Africa’s energy future required collaboration, investment, innovation, skills development and a deliberate commitment to building local industries. The summit attracted stakeholders, policymakers, investors, professionals and delegates from various African countries, with panel discussions focusing on collaboration, industrial capacity and strategies to strengthen energy security across the continent. items.title: Deux narcotrafiquants abattus dans l’extrême sud algérien
items.description: L’Algérie applique la tolérance zéro vis-à-vis des trafiquants de drogue. Mons d’une semaine après avoir abattu deux narcotrafiquants marocains vendredi 22 novembre, deux autres trafiquants ont été éliminés par l’armée mercredi 25 novembre cette fois à In Salah dans l’extrême sud de l’Algérie. « Dans la dynamique des efforts consentis pour sécuriser les frontières nationales et lutter contre la criminalité organisée et la contrebande, et grâce à l’exploitation optimale des renseignements, un détachement de l’Armée nationale populaire relevant du secteur militaire d’In Salah a éliminé mercredi 25 novembre, deux narcotrafiquants qui ont tenté de fuir et refusé d’obtempérer », a indiqué le MDN. Ces deux narcotrafiquants ont été tués alors qu’ils « tentaient d’introduire sur le territoire national une quantité importante de psychotropes de type prégabaline s’élevant à plus d’un million de comprimés », a ajouté la même source. Trafic de drogues : la mise en garde du MDN Deux détecteurs de métaux, deux véhicules tout terrain, deux téléphones satellitaires et deux appareils d’émission ont été saisis lors de cette opération. « Cette opération réaffirme la disponibilité des unités de l’Armée Nationale Populaire déployées à travers l’ensemble du territoire national pour faire face à ces réseaux criminels, et à mettre en échec leurs viles tentatives visant à inonder notre pays par ces poisons », a mis en garde le MDN. L’Algérie a considérablement durci la lutte contre le narcotrafic alors que d’importantes quantités de drogues et de psychotropes sont saisies annuellement dans le pays. L’article Deux narcotrafiquants abattus dans l’extrême sud algérien est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Labour Ministry and GIZ explore employment opportunities for Ghanaian youth in Germany
items.description: The Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment has engaged the German development agency, GIZ, to expand employment opportunities and establish safe migration pathways for Ghanaian youth seeking jobs in Germany. The discussions focused on strengthening labour migration and skills development partnerships, including opportunities under the Global Skills Partnership (GSP) and the German-African Global Skills Partnership programme. Speaking during the engagement, Leif Puschmann, Project Manager for the Skills Partnership Project at GIZ, outlined the organisation’s ongoing initiatives in Ghana, particularly those aimed at developing labour and skills pathways and promoting safe migration. He said one of the key areas being explored was the potential for employment opportunities in Germany’s construction sector, alongside assessing the interest of the Ministry, the Construction Association and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions. The initiative is being explored in collaboration with the German Employment Agency. The Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum, underscored the mutual benefits of the partnership, noting that German companies were ready to engage Ghanaian youth both remotely and within Germany. He stressed the need to sensitise German employers to the capabilities of Ghanaian professionals and ensure they recognise that the country’s workforce possesses skills comparable to those they seek from other labour markets. Promoting Ghanaian skills in Germany, strengthening cooperation on sustainability and increasing employer awareness were identified as key priorities for the partnership. Mr Agyekum also highlighted German language training as essential to preparing young Ghanaians to take advantage of the emerging opportunities. He called for German teachers to support language instruction for Ghanaian youth, including through remote learning arrangements. The Minister further emphasised the need to strengthen collaboration with technical and vocational institutions to equip young people with the relevant skills and prepare them for employment opportunities under the proposed labour pathways. The meeting was attended by the Head of the Ghana European Centre, Andreas Berding; Technical Adviser to the Skills Partnership Project, Emmanuel Hanson; and the project’s Technical Adviser and Coordinator, Dr Awudu Dramani Musah. Also present were the Ministry’s Chief Director, Hamidu Adakurugu Esq., alongside other directors and heads of departments.

items.title: Ex-BBC commentator Starmer-Smith dies aged 81
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former England scrum-half and renowned BBC rugby commentator Nigel Starmer-Smith has died aged 81 after a long battle with dementia. His son, Charlie, announced his death in a social media post on Thursday, saying he had “passed away peacefully this morning”. “Dad passed away peacefully this morning after a long battle with dementia,” Charlie wrote. Starmer-Smith was diagnosed with dementia in 2015. In 2021, Charlie described the condition as a major issue in sport and recalled how Covid-19 restrictions meant the family could only see his father through a window. The son also said head injuries were once treated as “like a badge of honour” in rugby and that dementia had affected other members of their family. Starmer-Smith played for Harlequins and the Barbarians and won seven England caps between 1969 and 1971. After retiring in 1976, he moved into broadcasting and journalism. He voiced the BBC’s Rugby Special highlights programme for 15 years and later commentated for ITV at the 2003 Rugby World Cup in Australia, where England won the title. In his tribute, Charlie described his father as “one of life’s great tourists” and remembered him as a player, commentator, writer, charity fundraiser, volunteer and family man. “He was a modest man and he’d hate for people to make a fuss,” Charlie wrote. “He loved to laugh but not as much as he loved to see others laughing.” He urged those who knew his father to think of a happy memory and smile, saying that was how he would remember him. items.title: 2027: Barau mobilises 3,405 Kano traditional rulers for APC
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has mobilised 3,405 traditional rulers in Kano State to support President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, himself and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The meeting, held at the Ali Jita Event Centre in Kano, brought together 3,032 ward heads, 347 village heads and 26 representatives and secretaries of district heads. According to a statement issued on Thursday by Barau’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the engagement was part of the senator’s ongoing consultations with stakeholders across Kano North Senatorial District. The meeting came barely 72 hours after Barau rallied more than 2,000 Islamic clerics from the 13 local government areas of the district to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Mudashir said the Deputy Senate President had, in recent months, intensified consultations with critical stakeholders across Kano North, urging them to support the President and all APC candidates. Barau commended the traditional rulers for their contributions to grassroots development, describing them as important partners in promoting peace, security and the wellbeing of their communities. He also appreciated their cooperation and prayers, saying traditional institutions remained closest to the people and understood their needs and challenges. On security, the senator acknowledged the challenges confronting some communities in Kano North but expressed optimism that the situation was improving through the collective efforts of security agencies and other stakeholders. He said the deployment of an Army battalion to Dambatta Local Government Area, in addition to existing security formations across the district, would strengthen security and protect lives and property. Highlighting electricity projects across the district, Barau said projects in Bichi, Dawanau Market and Kwanar Kanye in Kabo would cost more than N130 billion. “These projects may take time, but they will definitely turn around the economic fortunes of our senatorial district. I remember when I was in the House of Representatives between 1999 and 2003, similar power projects were attracted to Ogun State by the former President. Today, the state has become an industrial hub. We will get there in Kano North too,” he said. He said the electricity projects, alongside the Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo; Police Training School; Immigration Training School; and Civil Defence Training School, would stimulate economic activities, create jobs and accelerate development. In the health and education sectors, Barau disclosed plans to upgrade the Bagwai and Kabo hospitals into major referral and teaching hospitals, with the Kabo facility expected to serve as a teaching hospital for the Federal University of Science and Technology. He also said there were plans to upgrade the Federal College of Education, Bichi, and Audu Bako College of Agriculture, Dambatta, into universities, subject to the lifting of the existing embargo on the establishment and conversion of tertiary institutions. The senator urged the traditional rulers to encourage their subjects to vote for Tinubu, Governor Yusuf, himself and other APC candidates in 2027. He said Yusuf’s defection to the APC had strengthened cooperation between the Federal and Kano State governments, creating opportunities for the state to attract more federal projects and development interventions. Speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers, the Village Head of Lakwaya in Gwarzo Local Government Area, Alhaji Idris Ado Lakwaya, said they attended the meeting with the approval of the Kano Emirate Council. “We have the permission and approval of the Emir to attend this function. We thank the Deputy President of the Senate for his relentless efforts to address the challenges facing us, including insecurity,” he said. Barau meets Fulani association, persons with disabilities Meanwhile, Barau also met members of the Kano North Fulani Association and associations of persons with disabilities at the Amani Event Centre in Kano as part of his consultations with stakeholders across the district. Speaking at the meeting, former Senate Chief Whip, Senator Bello Hayatu Gwarzo, urged the groups to support Tinubu, Governor Yusuf, Barau and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Gwarzo commended Barau for engaging different groups and stakeholders across the district. “President Tinubu has already started well, and we are very optimistic that all his initiatives will bring the desired results that will benefit everyone. So, come out en masse and vote for him and all APC candidates from top to bottom,” he said. He dismissed the promises of opposition parties and urged residents to support the President. In his remarks, Barau reiterated his appeal for support for APC candidates, urging the groups to mobilise their members and other residents to vote for the party in the 2027 general elections. items.title: Onyesoh asks NASS to probe alleged assault on aides
items.description: …Says no aide should face violence for performing official duties By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Works, Senator Allwell Heacho Onyesoh (Rivers East), has called on the National Assembly management to urgently investigate the alleged assault on two of his principal aides by security operatives attached to the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations, Senator Olamilekan Adeola (Ogun West). The affected aides are Kingsley Wali, Esq., a Legislative Aide I, and Dr Kingsley Chioma Nwanyanwu, Special Adviser to the senator on General Services. Onyesoh called for a comprehensive investigation to identify the security operatives involved, preserve relevant closed-circuit television footage, establish the circumstances surrounding Wali’s injuries and investigate the alleged attempted arrest of Nwanyanwu. He also demanded protection for the two aides against intimidation or retaliation, insisting that the incident required a transparent investigation, accountability and justice for the victims. In a statement issued on Thursday and signed by his Special Adviser on Publicity and Communications, Peter Oriri, the senator strongly condemned the alleged assault, vowing not to tolerate any attempt to intimidate his aides or undermine their dignity. He maintained that no National Assembly official or aide should be subjected to violence or intimidation while performing legitimate official duties. According to him, the National Assembly must remain an institution governed by law, discipline and mutual respect, rather than a place where security operatives exercise arbitrary powers with impunity. The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday during a meeting of the Senate Committee on Appropriations at the National Assembly complex in Abuja. Wali was said to have sustained a head injury during a confrontation with security operatives attached to Adeola. Giving an account of the incident, Onyesoh’s office said the two aides were duly appointed officials who had accompanied their principal to the committee meeting and were leaving after he had entered the meeting room when the confrontation occurred. The statement said it was an established practice for legislative aides and other authorised officials to accompany their principals to committee meetings and see them off to the entrance. It added that the aides neither attempted to force their way into the meeting nor disrupt its proceedings. “For the avoidance of doubt, there was no closed-door session in progress when the incident occurred. Any suggestion that they were attempting to forcefully gain access to a restricted meeting is therefore unfounded,” the statement said. It alleged that security operatives stationed at the entrance physically restrained, pushed and slapped Nwanyanwu, despite his having no intention of entering the meeting. The statement further alleged that when Wali intervened, the operatives turned their aggression towards him. “During the assault, Barr. Wali was dragged towards the staircase, pushed down and struck on the head with the butt of a firearm. He sustained a serious head injury and emerged bleeding profusely, requiring urgent medical attention,” it added. Onyesoh’s office described the incident as a serious act of violence that should not be dismissed as a misunderstanding. It further alleged that the same security operatives subsequently restrained Nwanyanwu and attempted to arrest him while he was seeking medical assistance for his injured colleague. According to the statement, the operatives accused Nwanyanwu of being responsible for the incident. The senator’s office also questioned the authority of security personnel attached to the committee chairman to exercise powers over duly authorised National Assembly officials. It argued that such operatives were required to operate within established security protocols and could not usurp the institutional responsibilities of the Sergeant-at-Arms. The statement said Onyesoh, who was already seated in the committee meeting, immediately stepped out after being informed of the incident and brought the two affected aides before the committee. It added that senators present at the meeting condemned the alleged assault. Reiterating his demand for an investigation, Onyesoh said security responsibilities did not confer on operatives the right to assault, intimidate or unlawfully restrain anyone. The senator called on the appropriate National Assembly authorities to establish the facts surrounding the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that anyone found culpable was held accountable. items.title: El planeta cruza otra línea roja: una semana seguida por encima de los dos grados de calentamiento
items.description: Por primera vez, la Tierra ha registrado un calentamiento de más de 2 grados sobre las temperaturas de la época preindustrial durante una semana seguida. Al mismo tiempo que los países fracasan en la última cumbre del clima de Antalya (Turquía) y las potencias del mundo se muestran partidarias en Shenzhen de aumentar la producción de combustibles fósiles , el planeta sigue calentándose. Según ha confirmado el Servicio de Cambio Climático de Copernicus , se ha alcanzado la barrera de los 2 ºC en 10 días este mes de noviembre, siete de ellos de forma consecutiva. Y el lunes 23 de noviembre se produjo la diferencia más alta en la temperatura media global registrada hasta ahora, con un calentamiento de 2,25 °C por encima de la época preindustrial (1850-1900) y de 1,34 °C por encima del periodo 1991-2020. Seguir leyendo Qué significa una diferencia de 2 grados Dos grados de más en la temperatura respecto a la época preindustrial no parece mucho. Sin embargo, resulta algo enorme cuando se refiere a la temperatura media de la superficie de la Tierra. Para hacerse una idea mejor de lo que esto supone, está bien entender cómo se calcula. Cuando se habla de la temperatura media de un día, esto es la media de la temperatura registrada a lo largo de una jornada por puntos de todo el planeta, con sitios muy calurosos y otros muy fríos. Y cuando se habla de la temperatura media del año, es el promedio del globo, pero además a lo largo de los meses y las estaciones, tanto en invierno como en verano. En una media formada por valores tan diferentes, una pequeña diferencia supone un gran cambio.

items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Re1 per litre, diesel by Rs2 per litre
items.description: The government reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of diesel by Rs2 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs313 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs346 per litre on Nov 27 (Friday). The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively, as of price reductions made to both on Wednesday. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation. The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc. Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: «L’Europe se prépare à la guerre tout en exigeant un cessez-le-feu immédiat en Ukraine» : Lavrov dénonce les contradictions européennes
items.description: Sergueï Lavrov, a denonce, ce 26 novembre, la contradiction entre les appels a un cessez-le-feu immediat en Ukraine et les preparatifs militaires des capitales europeennes. Le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres s'exprimait lors d'une rencontre avec les participants au programme « Dialogue pour l'avenir » de la Fondation Gortchakov. Le lancement de l'operation militaire speciale a contraint l'Occident a abattre ses cartes, souligne Lavrov. Derriere leurs appels a un cessez-le-feu, les Europeens preparent le deploiement de contingents militaires et la creation de bases en Ukraine, sans chercher a parvenir a un reglement durable. C'est pourtant avec de telles ambitions qu'ils exigent de prendre part aux negociations entre Moscou, Washington et Kiev. Le chef de la diplomatie russe a egalement mis en cause l'intransigeance de Volodymyr Zelensky, qui persiste a rejeter les interets legitimes de la Russie et a reclamer l'adhesion de l'Ukraine a l'OTAN. Qualifiant l'insolence du chef du regime de Kiev de « marque de fabrique », le ministre a rappele les nombreuses concessions consenties par Moscou depuis 2003. Il a denonce la volonte de ceux qui continuent d'instrumentaliser l'Ukraine pour atteindre des objectifs irrealisables. Washington a l'ecoute des preoccupations securitaires de Moscou a la difference des dirigeants europeens, l'administration de Donald Trump fait preuve, selon Sergueï Lavrov, d'une « maturite politique » en maintenant le dialogue avec la Russie, malgre les divergences et les sanctions economiques visant notamment Rosneft et Lukoil. Le ministre a surtout souligne que Washington comprenait la necessite d'eliminer les causes profondes du conflit ukrainien, au premier rang desquelles figurent les menaces pesant sur la securite de la Russie a ses frontieres. L'Occident devra renoncer a sa politique de domination, selon Lavrov Revenant sur les relations russo-occidentales depuis la dissolution de l'Union sovietique, Sergueï Lavrov a rappele les efforts de rapprochement entrepris par Moscou, notamment a travers le Conseil Russie-OTAN et la cooperation avec l'Union europeenne. Selon lui, l'Occident a reduit a neant ces acquis en refusant a la Russie le droit de defendre ses interets legitimes. Le ministre a estime que, meme sans la question ukrainienne, les puissances occidentales auraient trouve un autre pretexte pour se soustraire a leurs engagements. Il a egalement denonce la volonte affichee de responsables europeens de maintenir les sanctions contre la Russie, meme apres la fin du conflit. Reprenant la metaphore du « jardin florissant » de Josep Borrell, Sergueï Lavrov a affirme que ce jardin commencait a pourrir, denoncant l'arrogance et la politique neocoloniale de l'Occident. Face a l'emergence d'un monde multipolaire, que le ministre considere comme ineluctable, les puissances occidentales devront renoncer a dicter leurs conditions au reste du monde et apprendre a negocier sur un pied d'egalite. Moscou, pour sa part, demeure ouvert au dialogue dans le respect mutuel.

items.title: Présidentielle 2027 : près d’«une centaine» de promesses de parrainages manquent toujours à Marine Le Pen
items.description: Moins de cinq mois avant le premier tour du scrutin presidentiel, la candidate pour l'heure donnee favorite par les sondages, avec plus de 30 % des intentions de vote, Marine Le Pen ne serait pas encore parvenue a obtenir 500 promesses de parrainages d'elus. « Il nous en manque un peu moins d'une centaine au moment ou on se parle », a declare le 26 novembre sur Europe 1 / CNews le porte-parole du Rassemblement national (RN), Laurent Jacobelli. « Mais on y va, on va y arriver », a poursuivi le depute de Moselle. C'est un scenario recurrent, pour le RN et avant lui le Front national : alors que la campagne presidentielle se profile, avec son obligation de presenter au Conseil constitutionnel 500 parrainages de maires, de parlementaires ou encore de conseillers departementaux et regionaux – issus d'au moins 30 departements – le parti a la flamme peine a obtenir les autographes des elus qui, en France, se comptent pourtant par dizaines de milliers. Parrainages du RN : "Il nous en manque un peu moins d'une centaine au moment où on se parle" déclare @ljacobelli #LaGrandeInterview #Europe1 https://t.co/frInLuGa15 — Europe 1 (@Europe1) November 26, 2026 « Je lance un appel aux maires qui ont envie que Marine Le Pen puisse etre candidate », avait indique au Parisien la presidente du groupe RN au Senat, Edwige Diaz, avant d'estimer qu'« a priori ca ne sera pas un sujet ». La raison de cette frilosite ? Les craintes de pressions que les ediles pourraient avoir a subir dans ledit « pays des droits de l'homme » et pretendument de la liberte d'opinion , une fois leur soutien au parti mariniste rendu public. « J'ai ma position politique, mais je ne veux pas qu'elle soit affichee au sein de ma mairie », a temoigne – sous couvert d'anonymat – un maire aupres de Public Senat. « ca creerait trop de grabuge de se positionner politiquement », a confie a la chaîne du Senat une edile sans etiquette d'un village de 80 habitants. Un « filtre », selon le Conseil constitutionnel Une reticence qui n'epargne pas les candidats percus comme plus « consensuels », a l'instar de Dominique de Villepin qui, en 2012, avait dû renoncer a la course a l'elysee faute d'avoir pu reunir suffisamment de soutiens. evoquant « un combat », l'ancien Premier ministre et chef de la diplomatie francaise a declare le 22 octobre sur le plateau de BFMTV avoir « depasse la barre des 300 signatures » d'elus. Deux semaines plus tot, sur Sud Radio, le macroniste Olivier Becht, qui affirme etre candidat pour que son fils et « sa generation ne revivent pas les horreurs que mes grands-parents ont connues au siecle dernier, avec les deux guerres mondiales », s'etait quant a lui declare « plutot confiant » dans la quete de signatures. Ce « filtre », comme l'a presente le Conseil constitutionnel, afin d'eviter les candidatures « trop marginales ou fantaisistes » , n'avait pas empeche en 2022 la maire de Paris, Anne Hidalgo, de se presenter a une presidentielle ou elle avait obtenu 1,7 % des suffrages ; « le score le plus bas de l'histoire du PS » a la presidentielle, comme avait titre Le Monde . Les equipes de l'edile parisienne n'avaient visiblement pas eu de difficulte a recueillir 1 440 signatures . Des parrainages que les pretendants a l'investiture supreme, pour l'edition 2027 de la course a l'elysee, ont jusqu'au 12 mars pour reunir.

items.title: Burkina : Le Premier ministre inaugure le siège de l’Université virtuelle du Faso et deux espaces numériques ouverts
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a procédé à l'inauguration du siège de l'Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso (UV-BF) et de ses espaces numériques ouverts, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. A travers ces infrastructures, le gouvernement ambitionne de renforcer les conditions d'apprentissage et de favoriser un accès plus large des jeunes à l'enseignement supérieur. Bâties sur les ressources propres de l’État, ces infrastructures s’inscrivent dans la volonté du Gouvernement de promouvoir une formation supérieure accessible, inclusive et de qualité. Elles ont été réalisées dans le cadre d’un investissement global de plus de 16 milliards de FCFA, qui prend également en compte les infrastructures de l’École polytechnique de Ouagadougou, l'amphithéâtre, et la crêche à l'Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo. Au cours de la cérémonie d'ouverture, le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a invité les enseignants à former des étudiants animés par l’esprit patriotique et engagés pour le développement du Burkina Faso. « Il ne sert à rien de former quelqu’un qui a la tête pleine avec le cœur vide de patriotisme » , a-t-il déclaré. Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo a également appelé à faire de la formation un levier de lutte contre la faim, les maladies et le retard technologique. Pour le ministre en charge de l’Enseignement supérieur, Pr Ardjima Thiombiano, ces réalisations permettront de doter les établissements concernés d’infrastructures adaptées à leurs ambitions. Il a notamment expliqué que le siège de l’UV-BF, construit sur quatre niveaux, constitue le centre de conception et de coordination des enseignements dispensés aux étudiants, tandis que les espaces numériques ouverts en sont les relais de proximité. Créée en 2018, l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso compte aujourd’hui 14 filières de formation, dont 10 licences et quatre masters, réparties dans trois unités de formation et de recherche. Pour l’année académique 2026-2027, elle accueille 16 634 étudiants, dont 52 % de femmes. Son personnel compte 122 agents, parmi lesquels 61 enseignants permanents. Depuis sa création, l’établissement a déjà formé 1 112 diplômés. Selon son Président, Dr Oumarou Zallé, ces nouvelles infrastructures, qui comprennent notamment un centre de données, un studio de production de contenus pédagogiques et des espaces de travail, permettront de mieux organiser les formations et d’accompagner le développement de l’enseignement à distance. À travers ce dispositif, le gouvernement entend rapprocher les services universitaires des apprenants. L’ambition affichée est de doter chaque région d’un espace numérique ouvert afin qu’aucun étudiant ne soit privé de formation supérieure en raison de l’éloignement géographique ou de difficultés sociales. Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: Why Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was overturned – FA panel
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Football Association has released the written reasons for overturning Leny Yoro’s red card for Manchester United against Liverpool, despite refereeing body Pro Ref maintaining that the on-field decision was not clearly wrong. According to Sky Sports, the FA’s independent regulatory commission unanimously ruled that referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” in deciding Liverpool striker Alexander Isak had an obvious goalscoring opportunity when Yoro fouled him during United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday. The panel said Isak’s touch was so heavy that he had lost control of the ball, allowing United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to close in and potentially gather it before the striker could shoot. “Taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity,” the commission said in its written reasons. The decision overturned Yoro’s one-match suspension, making the defender available for United’s Premier League match against Brentford on Saturday. Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb had defended the officials’ decision, saying Isak was moving quickly towards the ball and that it was “certainly not clearly wrong” to judge he would reach it before Lammens. United submitted video evidence from several angles, as well as footage of Brighton defender Pascal Struijk’s red card against Sunderland, which was overturned after an appeal. The club also argued that Isak would have been at least 1.8 metres short of the ball without Yoro’s challenge. The commission said it could not test the validity of United’s distance analysis and therefore viewed it with caution. A separate Premier League Key Match Incidents panel is reported to have backed the original decision; its findings for the matchweek are due to be published on December 2. The post Why Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was overturned – FA panel appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘A promise made is a promise kept’ – Agalga touts $12.7bn reserves

He said the reserves, recorded at the end of September 2026, provided approximately 4.5 months of import cover, which he contrasted with the three weeks he attributed to the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration. Speaking during the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, Mr Agalga said the figures demonstrated that the government had fulfilled its promise of improving the country’s external position and promoting currency stability. “Right Honourable Speaker, we promised a more stable currency and a stronger external position. Gross international reserves recorded 12.7 billion by the end of September, about 4.5 months of import cover. What is the record of the NPP? Your record in terms of import cover was just three weeks, three weeks. Now compare three weeks to 4.5 months of import cover. Mr Speaker, a promise made is a promise kept,” he said. Mr Agalga also commended Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson for what he described as a clear account of the government’s economic management. He used the opportunity to challenge former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta to return to Ghana and account for his eight-year tenure. “Dr Cassiel Ato Forson accounted for his stewardship with grace and courage; we call upon Ken Ofori-Atta to come back home. He should return to this country and account for his stewardship for the eight years that he superintended over the finances and the economy of this country,” he added.

items.title: Achakzai's proposal of national govt only solution to political, constitutional crisis: TTAP
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday maintained that forming a national government is the only solution to the country’s ongoing political and constitutional crisis. Earlier this week, TTAP Chairman and National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai had called for the formation of a national government and comprehensive constitutional and political reforms to steer the country out of the mounting crises. However, the main opposition party, the PTI, has distanced itself from Achakzai’s proposal. A joint meeting of its parliamentary groups discussed the matter, and a majority of the members opposed the idea, according to one participant. Speaking to Dawn on Thursday, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai argued that a national government would pave the way for the release of PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, who has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023. However, Yousafzai made it clear that the proposed arrangement could not be imposed or negotiated behind closed doors. TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai. — Photo via X/File He stressed that all political forces, particularly PTI and its founder, must be part of consultations before any decision on the formation of a national government. However, he warned that excluding any political force would undermine the democratic legitimacy of a possible national government. “The political uncertainty cannot be overcome through political victimisation or unilateral decisions, but requires serious and meaningful dialogue among all political parties, democratic stakeholders and the establishment,” the TTAP spokesperson stated. “The proposal for a national government is neither directed against any political party nor intended to provide political advantage to any particular group,” he affirmed, describing it as an effort to restore public confidence in democratic institutions and end political polarisation. Under the proposed framework, the first priority would be restoration of a democratic environment in which “fundamental rights, constitutional freedoms, freedom of expression and political activities” are protected, Yousafzai said. He added that such an arrangement would allow all the parties to participate in peaceful political activities without discrimination. The TTAP spokesperson also called for making the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) independent under a mutually agreed, credible and non-partisan chief election commissioner who enjoyed the confidence of all major political parties. Yousafzai said the proposed national government should ensure free, fair and transparent general elections across the country in accordance with the Constitution so that the people’s actual mandate was reflected in the composition of the elected government. He also called for a multi-party conference to be convened before the formation of the proposed government. The meeting, he said, should focus exclusively on reaching a consensus over the mechanism, framework and necessary arrangements for holding credible elections and establishing a genuinely representative government. The TTAP spokesperson cautioned that the national government must not become an alternative to the people’s mandate or a permanent political arrangement. Its sole purpose should be to facilitate elections and transfer power to representatives chosen by the electorate, he emphasised. “Pakistan needs neither an imposed political arrangement nor a government established through political expediency,” he said, adding that the authority to govern must flow exclusively from the free and fair vote of the people. He said the ultimate objective should be a country governed under one Constitution, an independent electoral system and a government that genuinely represented the will of the people.

items.title: Recherche scientifique et technologique: de nouvelles infrastructures pour l’Ecole polytechnique de Ouagadougou
items.description: Après l’inauguration du siège de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso et de deux Espaces numériques ouverts (ENO), le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a poursuivi, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, la série d’inaugurations avec celle des nouvelles infrastructures de l’École polytechnique de Ouagadougou (EPO), situées dans le quartier de Nagrin. Ces réalisations renforcent les capacités d’accueil et les moyens de formation pratique de l’établissement. ‎Quatre infrastructures ont été inaugurées : un bâtiment pédagogique de type R+3, réalisé pour un coût de 1 317 463 757 FCFA TTC, comprenant des salles de cours, des bureaux administratifs et des espaces de réunion, pour une capacité totale de 2 000 places assises ; un bâtiment abritant 14 laboratoires de travaux pratiques et une salle multimédia, réalisé pour 587 millions de FCFA TTC ; un atelier de génie mécanique, d’un coût de 150 millions de FCFA TTC ; et un atelier de génie textile, d’une valeur de 57 millions de FCFA TTC, partiellement équipé pour la filature, le tissage et le tricotage. ‎Pour le ministre chargé de l’Enseignement supérieur, le Pr Ardjouma Thiombiano, cette inauguration marque une étape importante dans le développement de l’EPO. Depuis sa création, l’établissement fonctionnait dans des bâtiments loués, pour une charge d’environ 12 millions de FCFA par mois. Selon le ministre, ces nouvelles infrastructures permettront à l’État de mettre fin à cette dépense récurrente tout en offrant à l’école un cadre de formation adapté à ses ambitions. ‎L’École polytechnique de Ouagadougou compte environ 659 élèves ingénieurs inscrits et forme des cadres dans plusieurs domaines, notamment les technologies et l’informatique. Depuis sa création, elle a contribué à la formation et à l’insertion de près de 104 ingénieurs dans le tissu socio-économique national. Le ministre a également annoncé une prochaine phase de développement de l’EPO, conformément aux orientations du Chef de l’État. ‎À travers ces réalisations, le Gouvernement réaffirme son engagement en faveur d’un enseignement supérieur axé sur la formation pratique et le développement des compétences scientifiques et technologiques de la jeunesse burkinabè DCRP/Primature L’article Recherche scientifique et technologique: de nouvelles infrastructures pour l'Ecole polytechnique de Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Children demand stronger action to protect their rights at National Children’s Parliament
items.description: Children from across Ghana have called for stronger action to protect their rights, urging government and stakeholders to translate commitments to their welfare into tangible improvements in their lives. The demand was made at the 8th session of the National Children’s Parliament in Accra, held at the GNAT Hall to mark the 2026 World Children’s Day. Organised by the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection in collaboration with Plan International Ghana and other stakeholders, the session brought together young representatives to deliberate on challenges confronting children and advocate for stronger protection. Country Director of Plan International Ghana, Muniratu Issifu, said the participation of 20 children from underserved communities in the North East, Upper West, Volta and Oti Regions ensured that the concerns of rural children were represented. She said children in these communities continued to face child marriage, child labour, teenage pregnancy, limited access to quality education and violence. Mrs Issifu urged government and stakeholders to ensure resolutions from the parliament translated into concrete action, rather than remaining unimplemented declarations. “Let this 8th session of the National Children’s Parliament not end with speeches, applause and resolutions that gather dust. Let it mark the beginning of renewed national commitments to protect every child in Ghana,” she said. She also called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies to prioritise child protection in their development plans and budgets, reminding the young parliamentarians that their voices mattered in shaping the country’s future. “You are not the leaders of tomorrow, you are the leaders of today. Do not underestimate the power of your voices,” she said. Acting Director of the Ministry, Alexander Boadu Sefah, reaffirmed government’s commitment to ending violence against children by 2030, saying efforts were underway to address harmful social practices, strengthen support services, create safer environments and enforce child protection laws. He, however, acknowledged that harmful sociocultural practices and inadequate financial resources remained major obstacles. UNICEF Representative in Ghana, Andy Brooks, meanwhile, warned of growing online threats, including exploitation, cyberbullying and pressure on children to share compromising photographs. He said UNICEF was collaborating with the Cyber Security Authority to educate children on online safety and urged victims of disturbing online experiences to contact the Authority on 292 for assistance. Mr Brooks also disclosed that Ghana had only 43 per cent of the social workers required to meet its child protection needs, calling for stronger enforcement of existing laws. “One of the discrepancies we’ve been talking about today is that sometimes there’s a distance between the law and the reality on the ground,” he said. The young parliamentarians are demanding that authorities move beyond assurances to deliver effective protection against abuse, harmful practices and online exploitation, and ensure children’s voices influence decisions affecting their wellbeing.

items.title: Élections locales : ces véhicules et trains interdits de circuler
items.description: La circulation des camions-citernes et des véhicules transportant des matériaux de construction ainsi que les trains de marchandises sera interdite, à partir du 27 novembre à minuit jusqu’au 29 novembre prochains. La Gendarmerie nationale a annoncé, ce jeudi 26 novembre, des mesures de restriction concernant la circulation des véhicules de transport des matériaux de construction et des carburants, lors des élections locales du 28 novembre prochain. « La circulation de tout véhicule affecté au transport de marchandises (gravier, sable, bois et ses dérivés, ainsi que tout autre matériau de construction), et des camions-citernes transportant du carburant, est interdite durant la période allant du 27 novembre 2026 à 00 h 00 jusqu'au 29 novembre 2026 à 05 h 00 du matin », a annoncé la gendarmerie dans un communiqué publié sur sa page Facebook Tariki. « Cette interdiction s'applique également au transport de marchandises par voie ferroviaire durant la même période », a ajouté la même source. Les véhicules de transport de produits alimentaires non concernés Les véhicules assurant le transport des produits alimentaires ne sont pas concernés par ces restrictions exceptionnelles. « Sont exemptés de cette mesure les véhicules assurant l'approvisionnement courant de la population en denrées alimentaires (lait, farine, viande, fruits et légumes, etc.) », a précisé la gendarmerie. Il a été indiqué en outre que « le wali territorialement compétent peut accorder des autorisations exceptionnelles pour la circulation et le transport par camions-citernes de carburant ». Cette mesure, rappelle la Gendarmerie, a été prise conformément à l'arrêté du 16 novembre 2026, émis par le ministère de l'Intérieur et des Collectivités locales, relatif à la circulation des véhicules de transport de marchandises durant la période allant du 27 au 29 novembre 2026. L’article Élections locales : ces véhicules et trains interdits de circuler est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Dr Ayine’s directive: When the State enforces the constitution against itself
items.description: For more than three decades, Ghana’s 1992 Constitution has guaranteed the rights of persons suspected or accused of crime. Yet successive governments have struggled to translate these textual guarantees into lived realities for the ordinary Ghanaian. We have lost count of the occasions on which persons under investigation have suffered serious violations of their rights, with little by way of tangible remedy. While our search for a solution to this problem has occasioned very little success in the past, the Attorney-General, Dr Dominic Ayine, may have untied, or at least begun to loosen, this Gordian knot by his 2 November 2026 recent Directive on Constitutional and Legal Compliance in the Conduct of Criminal Investigations, addressed to all public bodies with powers to investigate criminal offences. The Directive has received commendation from the public generally. However, some notable public voices have sought to downplay it as a mere restatement of existing constitutional text. Admittedly, the language of the Directive echoes several existing provisions of the Constitution. That does not, however, make it any less a reform. From its first word, the Directive identifies serious defects in the way crimes are investigated and prosecuted and prescribes considered measures to correct them. Its significance lies not in the novelty of its content but in its attempt to confront the gap between “rights on paper” and “rights in practice”, one of the most entrenched problems of Ghana’s constitutional democracy. Since the inception of the Fourth Republic, a wide gulf has persisted between the fundamental human rights guaranteed in our Constitution and the administrative culture within which they are supposed to be enjoyed. Two factors account for this. The first is that Ghana’s constitutional architecture favours remedial over preventive constitutionalism. The Constitution codifies an extensive catalogue of rights but leaves their enforcement almost entirely to the judiciary, which can remedy a breach after it occurs but can rarely prevent it. The second account is cultural. Under Article 12(1) of the 1992 Constitution, all organs of government and their agencies are mandated to respect and uphold fundamental human rights. Yet we have developed a culture in which constitutional rights are treated largely as matters for lawyers and judges, rather than as considerations that must inform the everyday exercise of public power. The limitations of judicial rights protection Ghana’s Constitution provides judicial and quasi-judicial mechanisms for redress for human rights breaches. In reality, the courts have assumed the role of the principal arena for rights protection. This arrangement, a constitutional democracy in which the courts become the first port of call for securing respect for fundamental human rights, is inherently problematic. It hands administrators and investigators something close to a blank cheque to breach rights, and by the time the courts intervene, the right holder may have suffered harm that no compensation can undo. This is especially so when the breach involves unlawful detention. A person unlawfully detained cannot recover the days of liberty lost, however much in damages is eventually awarded. Beyond this is the economic reality of accessing justice. From securing the services of a lawyer to paying filing fees, litigation is often financially and temporally prohibitive. This places the constitutionally guaranteed remedy beyond the reach of the people it seeks to protect. The result is that for many Ghanaians, the violation of their constitutional rights is an unfortunate experience from which they must simply move on without any remedy. But even for those who can pursue a remedy, a favourable judgment may vindicate their rights without dismantling the institutional culture that occasioned the violation. This is especially so when the state shoulders the cost for the officials whose direct conduct led to the breach of rights, with little to no individual responsibility. The reality is an environment where we have conflated having a right, enjoying that right, and obtaining a remedy for its violation. We have interpreted human rights guarantees to mean only obtaining a remedy for their violation, even though the constitutional promise is the enjoyment of fundamental human rights, not merely the opportunity to litigate their violations. The posturing of our courts has also not always helped. There have been progressive judicial interventions, including the Supreme Court’s decision in Martin Kpebu v Attorney-General , which struck down the statutory denial of bail for certain offences. Yet the manner in which courts sometimes exercise their discretion in bail and remand applications, their tolerance of delayed prosecutions, and the general approach, reflected in Raphael Cubagee v Michael Yeboah Asare , that relevant evidence is not excluded merely because it was improperly obtained, have together contributed to the fossilisation of a culture of disregard for constitutional rights. Where investigators can achieve their objectives notwithstanding the constitutional impropriety of the means employed, disregard for fundamental human rights risks becoming institutionally rational. The significance of Ayine’s Directive It is against this backdrop that the Attorney-General’s Directive is a breath of fresh air. The Directive addresses several practices that have regrettably become familiar features of our criminal justice system, including detention beyond the constitutional 48-hour limit (which, it clarifies, runs from the moment a person’s liberty is first restricted, not from when an arrest is entered in a station diary), the use of investigative powers to recover civil debts, unreasonable bail conditions, coerced confessions and the public parading of suspects. In my view though, the most consequential provision in the Directive is the Attorney-General’s decision to withhold its authority from prosecutions that rest on evidence obtained through torture or coercion. The Attorney-General contemplates discontinuing prosecutions tainted by such serious violations. By adopting this policy approach, the Attorney-General has introduced prosecutorial consequences for investigative misconduct even before the question of admissibility reaches the courtroom. In effect, and for the first time in our constitutional history, the state is declaring that it is not interested in securing convictions at any constitutional cost. Beyond the publication of the Directive While we remain optimistic that the Directive would catalyse significant criminal justice reforms, that optimism cannot obscure the fact that it confronts an entrenched institutional culture. Ghana is not particularly impoverished in progressive constitutional and statutory prescriptions. What we have struggled with is translating them into institutional behaviour. The Directive commendably provides for quarterly compliance reports, weekly inspection of custody registers by station and unit commanders, mandatory training and disciplinary action against officers in breach. I would further propose that the Attorney-General establish a standing working committee to oversee implementation, undertake compliance audits and periodically publish its findings. It must provide an accessible complaint mechanism that allows citizens to report violations outside the context of litigation. Aggregated outcomes of such complaints and their investigation should be published alongside the quarterly compliance reports, so that the public can see whether complaints lead anywhere. Additionally, the Attorney-General’s office must also deliberately engage in nationwide training of investigating officers on the Directives and the Constitution. We must ultimately recognise that the aspiration of constitutionalism is not to build a society in which citizens become adept at litigating the violations of their rights. It is to build one in which the exercise of public power is so thoroughly informed by constitutional values that the need for such litigation becomes exceptional. We must move from a culture in which citizens invoke the Constitution against the state to one in which the state invokes the Constitution against its own excesses. Dr Ayine’s Directive offers us an opportunity to begin that transition. For now, the Attorney-General deserves his flowers. Whether he keeps them will depend on how persistently the Directive is enforced. – By Noah Ephraem Adamtey, President, Young Lawyers Forum of the Ghana Bar Association.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Building a culture of ownership and high performance
items.description: Insight. High-performing organisations are built by people who understand their responsibilities, take ownership of outcomes and remain committed to delivering results. A culture of ownership develops when employees are empowered to act, managers provide clear direction and leaders consistently reinforce accountability. The CEO must ensure that organisational performance is not driven only by instructions from the top. People at every level should understand how their work contributes to the organisation’s strategic priorities and accept responsibility for the quality and results of their contribution. Ownership also requires an environment where employees have the authority, resources and support needed to perform. Accountability without empowerment creates frustration, while empowerment without accountability creates inconsistency. Effective leadership brings both together. Key Strategies: Clarify expectations: Ensure that every employee understands their responsibilities and performance targets. Connect roles to strategy: Help teams see how their individual contributions influence organisational objectives. Empower decision-making: Give employees appropriate authority to solve problems and take responsibility within defined boundaries. Recognise performance: Reward initiative, collaboration, innovation and consistent delivery of results. Address underperformance: Deal with performance gaps promptly through coaching, support and clear accountability measures. CEO Leadership Actions. Review whether departmental and individual performance targets align with the organization’s strategic priorities. Encourage executives to delegate meaningful responsibilities while maintaining clear accountability for outcomes. Introduce regular performance conversations to recognize achievements, address challenges, and agree on improvement actions. Actionable Tip. Ask every executive to identify one area where decision-making can be moved closer to the people doing the work, with clear performance measures and accountability. Why This Matters? A culture of ownership improves execution, reduces unnecessary dependence on senior management and strengthens organizational responsiveness. It also creates a workforce that takes initiative, solves problems and remains focused on results. High performance becomes sustainable when accountability is shared across the organisation. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu
items.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communication of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as politicians with the best experience in governance ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Momodu said the duo had the experience and capacity to tackle Nigeria’s challenges, expressing confidence that Atiku could revive moribund industries, including the Ajaokuta Steel Company, by engaging competent professionals. He spoke in an interview on Trust TV on Thursday, while defending Atiku’s ability to deliver on his promises if elected president in 2027. Momodu said he believed in Atiku’s leadership ability, citing his success in business and willingness to deploy expertise in addressing difficult national challenges. “Nothing is impossible with the determination of a leader, and I know Alhaji Atiku Abubakar to be a very different kind of leader, and that’s why he’s been able to run his own business successfully,” he said. The ADC chieftain said Atiku’s promise to revamp the Ajaokuta Steel Company should not be interpreted as a plan to repeat past approaches, but as an opportunity to bring in professionals with the requisite expertise to restore the facility. “If he tells you that he will revamp Ajaokuta, it does not mean that he will do it the way they did it decades ago. He will bring in the best expert,” Momodu said. He cited the revival of Nigeria’s railway system under the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari as an example of how leadership and competent personnel could transform infrastructure previously considered beyond recovery. Momodu credited Amaechi, who served as Minister of Transportation under Buhari, with delivering railway projects that restored public confidence in train transportation across parts of the country. “You can see even while President Buhari was in power, there was a man who was able to do and deliver so many projects, and that man is the Right Honourable Chibuke Rotimi Amaechi,” he said. According to Momodu, Nigerians had previously lost hope in the railway system but became proud of the trains following the projects executed during Amaechi’s tenure. “People gave up on our trains, that the railways will never function again in Nigeria. But you can see within a short time, we were all very proud to show off our trains as they moved in different parts of Nigeria,” he said. He expressed optimism that a combination of Atiku’s experience and Amaechi’s record in infrastructure development would deliver better governance if they worked together in 2027. “So the same thing will happen if you bring in Atiku Amaechi together in 2027. These guys have the best experience in governance,” Momodu added. The post 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana records average of 100 fire outbreaks weekly – Interior Minister
items.description: Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak has disclosed that Ghana records an average of 100 fire outbreaks every week, with incidents increasing during the peak fire season between October and February. He has warned that the recurring outbreaks are inflicting significant economic losses on the country and called for stricter compliance with fire safety regulations to protect lives, property and businesses. He made the disclosure in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, during deliberations on the 2027 Budget, following a fire outbreak at the Accra Timber Market on Wednesday, November 25, which destroyed goods and threatened several shops. According to Mr Mohammed-Mubarak, the scale of fire incidents recorded across the country remains a major concern, particularly during the dry season when outbreaks become more frequent. “On average, there are 100 fires across our country a week. That tells you the extent of how we’re burning our economy. So, on average, you have in a month sometimes as many as over 1,500 fires, especially around this time, from October all the way to February,” he told Parliament. He said the figures demonstrate the urgent need for individuals, businesses and property owners to take fire safety seriously, adding that preventable outbreaks continue to expose the country to substantial economic losses. As part of efforts to improve compliance with fire safety requirements, the Interior Minister announced the introduction of the Automatic Fire Compliance and Safety System (AFCAS), an automated platform designed to simplify the process of obtaining fire safety certificates. Mr Mohammed-Mubarak explained that the previous certification process was largely manual, making it difficult for property owners to secure the necessary documentation and contributing to low compliance levels. He noted that fire certification was particularly important for property owners seeking financial assistance from banks, as lenders often require evidence that buildings meet the necessary safety standards. “We’ve introduced what we call the AFCAS, that’s Automatic Fire Compliance and Safety System. Where before now, when you want to take a loan, they want to be sure that your house is certified, that you’ve taken a fire certificate. It used to be very manual, and a lot of people were not complying,” he said. The Minister said the new system, which commenced in November 2026, was intended to make certification more accessible while encouraging property owners to ensure their buildings meet the required fire safety standards. He urged households, commercial property owners and businesses to take advantage of the platform by registering their buildings for the necessary assessment and certification. “With the introduction of AFCAS, that also started at the beginning of this month. We will encourage each of us to be able to subscribe and make sure that your buildings are certified and assisted to ensure that when there’s a fire, at least something could be done,” he added. The Minister’s disclosure comes against the backdrop of recurring fire outbreaks at markets and commercial centres, where traders frequently suffer significant losses through the destruction of goods, shops and other business assets. The latest incident at the Accra Timber Market has once again highlighted the vulnerability of trading centres to fire disasters and the need for effective preventive measures. For many traders, such incidents result in the loss of livelihoods and capital, while also disrupting commercial activities and affecting the wider economy. Mr Mohammed-Mubarak’s comments point to the government’s intention to strengthen fire prevention through improved certification and greater compliance with safety standards. The introduction of AFCAS is expected to help address some of the challenges associated with the existing certification process and encourage building owners to take greater responsibility for fire safety. With the peak fire season running from October to February, the Minister’s warning places renewed emphasis on the need for preventive action to reduce the frequency of outbreaks and limit their devastating consequences.

items.title: Éventuelle annulation de l’Aïd Al-Adha : Belfkih précise la position du gouvernement
items.description: À quelques mois de l’Aïd Al-Adha, la question du cheptel national et de la disponibilité du bétail pour la fête religieuse suscite de nouvelles interrogations. Alors que plusieurs médias nationaux ont relayé, mercredi, des informations faisant état d’une éventuelle annulation de l’Aïd Al-Adha, sur la base de sources gouvernementales, le porte-parole du gouvernement, Samir Belfkih, a assuré que cette hypothèse n’avait pas été examinée par l’Exécutif. Interpellé sur le sujet, ce jeudi, lors de la conférence de presse organisée à l’issue du Conseil de gouvernement, le responsable a été invité à préciser si le gouvernement avait effectivement discuté de la possibilité d’annuler la célébration et quelles mesures avaient été prises à cet égard. « Je tiens à vous confirmer, et je le répète, que cette question n’est pas à l’ordre du jour », a répondu Samir Belfkih, écartant ainsi l’existence de discussions gouvernementales sur une éventuelle annulation de la fête. Le porte-parole a précisé que la priorité actuelle de l’Exécutif portait sur la reconstitution du cheptel national. Dans ce cadre, les efforts concernent notamment la gestion des importations de viande, avec pour objectif de faire baisser les prix sur le marché national. Il a également évoqué l’évaluation de l’ensemble de cette opération. S’agissant de l’Aïd Al-Adha, Samir Belfkih a souligné qu’il restait encore cinq mois avant cette échéance, estimant qu’il était, à ce stade, prématuré de s’en préoccuper. The post Éventuelle annulation de l’Aïd Al-Adha : Belfkih précise la position du gouvernement appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘This is the people’s budget’ – Agalga defends 2027 budget, rules out new taxes
items.description: Majority Leader James Agalga has defended the 2027 Budget as a “people’s budget”, saying it delivers on the government’s promises to reduce inflation, borrowing and excessive public spending without introducing new taxes. Contributing to the closing debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, 2026, Agalga said the government would also fund major infrastructure projects without resorting to additional borrowing. “Indeed, it is the people’s budget. Let me say that again, this is the people’s budget. No new taxes, no borrowing for the Accra-Kumasi Expressway, no borrowing for the Western Corridor Railway Line,” he stated. Agalga said the budget challenged the notion that economic progress must come at the expense of increased public debt and financial hardship for citizens. “For too long our people have been told that progress must come with pain, that development must be financed by more debt, and that the only way to move this country forward is to load the next generation with more loans. This budget rejects this thinking. It is a budget of restraint with purpose. It is a budget that says we can build without mortgaging tomorrow,” he stated. The Majority Leader said the government had fulfilled its commitments to reduce inflation, curb excessive spending and lower borrowing. “We promised to bring inflation down. We have delivered. Inflation stood at 5.5% in October. That is 2.5 percentage points lower than the 8% recorded in October last year,” he said. He also cited the public debt stock, which he said stood at GH¢759.3 billion, equivalent to 47.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), at the end of October. “We promised to cut profligate spending, and we have delivered. We promised to reduce borrowing. We have delivered,” he added. The government has pointed to improvements in key macroeconomic indicators, including declining inflation and relative stability in the exchange rate, as evidence of progress in its economic management. The Minority, however, has argued that these gains have yet to translate into sufficient relief for ordinary Ghanaians, particularly households and small businesses facing persistent cost-of-living pressures. The debate on the 2027 Budget is expected to conclude with a vote in Parliament.
