items.title: Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation commits US$135m to lifesaving care across Africa
items.description: The Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity has announced a US$135 million commitment to expand access to essential medicines, medical equipment and health technologies in nine African countries, including Ghana. The initiative will help governments improve maternal and newborn survival and strengthen primary healthcare. The foundation announced the commitment at the International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA) in Addis Ababa. The investment will benefit more than 500 health facilities in Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Nigeria, Rwanda, Ghana, Sierra Leone and Mozambique. The foundation expects its commitment to mobilise more than US$550 million in additional financing through matched contributions from partner governments and donors. Each participating government will contribute at least as much as the foundation commits to its country, extending the investment’s reach. For a pregnant woman experiencing complications or a premature baby struggling to breathe, access to the right medicines and equipment can save a life. Yet many hospitals and clinics in low- and middle-income countries lack the essential supplies they need to provide timely, quality care. Her Excellency Dr Shamma Khalifa Al Mazrouei, Director General of the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity, said the initiative would help health workers get the supplies they need to care for patients. “In partnership with countries, we are working towards a future where no mother, newborn, or child dies from a preventable cause. Skilled health workers are essential to this vision, but their ability to save and improve lives depends on having ready access to the medicines and equipment they need. Across Africa, governments are investing in health systems and the people who deliver care. We welcome this opportunity to work together to ensure health workers have reliable access to the tools they need to deliver better outcomes for patients and communities.” Persistent supply shortages delay treatment and undermine progress in many health systems. Across Africa, public health facilities have essential medicines available in only 35 per cent of cases, and fewer than a third of facilities are equipped to carry out basic diagnostic tests. To address these shortages, African governments are increasingly combining donor funding with domestic resources under national health plans. The approach helps countries expand and maintain supplies of medicines and other essential health commodities. Ethiopia The foundation was the first to commit funding to Ethiopia’s Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) Compact, pledging US$20 million. The pledge helped secure a further US$151.2 million from development partners. The Ethiopian government matched the combined contributions, bringing total funding to US$342.4 million to strengthen maternal, newborn and child health services nationwide. Over three years, the funding will equip about 120 health facilities across Ethiopia with lifesaving supplies. These include AI-enabled ultrasound equipment to help health workers quickly detect and respond to complications during pregnancy and childbirth, as well as antibiotics to reduce sepsis risk. Dr Mekdes Daba, Ethiopia’s Minister of Health, said the compact would improve access to essential supplies and strengthen services for women, newborns, and children. “Ethiopia has consistently prioritised the advancement of reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health within its broader health sector transformation agenda. The RMNCH Compact advances this commitment through a new partnership model built on shared investment and mutual accountability. “This partnership will strengthen service delivery, improve the availability of essential medicines and health commodities, and reinforce the services that women, newborns and children rely on. Our aim is simple: fewer preventable deaths among mothers, newborns and children, wherever they live in Ethiopia.” Rwanda In Rwanda, the foundation’s US$15 million commitment will provide essential equipment to 170 health facilities, including district and teaching hospitals, and help mobilise a further US$40 million in financing. The investment builds on Rwanda’s efforts to make childbirth safer and improve newborn care. It will provide tools to help health workers manage postpartum bleeding, as well as incubators and respiratory support equipment for small, sick newborns. The Honourable Dr Sabin Nsanzimana, Rwanda’s Minister of Health, said a reliable supply of medicines and equipment would help the country sustain its progress in maternal and child health. “Over the past two decades, Rwanda has transformed maternal and child health, bringing quality care within reach of more families. Sustaining these gains depends not only on skilled professionals and health facilities, but on a reliable supply of the medicines, equipment, and technologies they need to deliver care. “Our partnership with the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity builds on Rwanda’s longstanding investment in health. Together, we are working to ensure that the progress we have achieved translates into healthier futures for every mother, newborn, and child.” Liberia The foundation’s US$10 million commitment to Liberia, matched by donor funding, will support the country’s national referral teaching hospital and connected facilities to improve care for women, newborns and children. The funding will provide lifesaving technologies to help health workers manage complicated births, stabilise critically ill newborns and children, and diagnose conditions more quickly at the bedside. It will also fund clinical mentorship to help doctors, nurses and midwives use the new equipment confidently in their daily work. The investment will build national expertise in biomedical engineering so that the equipment can be maintained and repaired for years to come. Her Excellency Dr Louise Mapleh Kpoto, Liberia’s Minister of Health, said the partnership would improve referral services and strengthen health workers’ skills. “Liberia is committed to strengthening its health system so that everyone can access quality care, wherever they live. Our partnership with the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity will support this commitment by enhancing services at our referral hospitals and strengthening the skills of our health workers. Together, we are improving care for our people today and preparing our health system to meet the needs of tomorrow.”

items.title: FG targets $200m trade with Tunisia by 2028
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has proposed a $200 million bilateral trade target with Tunisia by 2028 and supported moves to establish direct flights between both countries to boost trade, tourism and people-to-people relations. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the proposal when Tunisia’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Antit Moshen, visited him in Abuja on Tuesday. In a statement on Thursday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Enikanolaiye identified direct air connectivity as a key factor in strengthening economic and diplomatic relations between the two countries. He said direct flights would facilitate trade and tourism, promote educational exchanges and strengthen ties between Nigerians and Tunisians. The minister also called for greater private-sector participation in bilateral economic relations, urging Nigerian companies, including the Dangote Group, to explore investment opportunities in Tunisia. Speaking during the meeting, Moshen disclosed that bilateral trade between Nigeria and Tunisia had increased from $7 million to more than $100 million by 2024. He identified the absence of direct flights as a major obstacle to deeper bilateral relations, assuring that Tunisia was committed to addressing the challenge. The Tunisian ambassador also reaffirmed his country’s commitment to maintaining its annual scholarship allocation for Nigerian students. In response, Enikanolaiye said he would work with relevant government institutions to facilitate access to the scholarship opportunities for eligible Nigerians. He also called for increased cooperation between both countries in French-language education. The minister further expressed Nigeria’s readiness to work towards convening the sixth session of the Nigeria–Tunisia Joint Commission in the first quarter of 2027. He said the meeting would provide an opportunity for both countries to review their bilateral relations, strengthen cooperation and address outstanding issues. items.title: Senate probes LPG exports over domestic supply shortage
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has raised concerns over inadequate supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the domestic market, warning that the shortfall could undermine efforts to reduce the price of cooking gas in the country. The Senate Committee on Gas Resources, chaired by Senator Jarigbe Jarigbe (APC, Cross River North), raised the concern on Thursday during an interface with stakeholders in the gas sector on export revenue remittances and domestic LPG supply. The meeting, held at the National Assembly complex, Abuja, was convened to examine the availability of LPG in the domestic market, export volumes and revenue remittances from the country’s gas sector. Jarigbe said the situation was contrary to the objectives of Presidential Executive Order 9, signed by President Bola Tinubu on February 13, 2026, which seeks to improve oil and gas revenue remittances to the Federation Account. He said the government also needed to ensure adequate domestic gas supply to reduce the financial burden on Nigerians. “LPG has to be supplied to the domestic market for the good of the common man as intended with Executive Order 9 issued by President Tinubu to ameliorate the sufferings of the masses on price of gas,” he said. The executive order, however, focuses primarily on oil and gas revenue remittances rather than expressly mandating domestic LPG supply. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, the lawmaker said the committee was determined to establish the reasons for the inadequate supply and work towards bringing down cooking gas prices. “We are already working for Nigerians here, for our people, and that’s why we want to get to the root of it. “And we’ll make sure that the price of gas goes down, because when there is adequate supply in response to demand, the price will naturally go down,” he said. Jarigbe said industry operators had attributed the export of some LPG to the ratio of propane to butane in the product. He, however, argued that the composition could be adjusted through blending to make more of the product suitable for domestic consumption. “They give an excuse that the ratio of propane to butane is 80-20, and that’s what they export. But it’s a matter of blending, so that it will be the reverse: the quantity of butane will be 80 per cent, while the quantity of propane will be 20 per cent for local consumption in Nigeria,” he said. During the meeting, the Deputy Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service in charge of Tariff and Trade, Caroline Kemen Niagwan, presented the agency’s records of LPG exports. Niagwan said 190.8 metric tonnes of LPG were exported in 2024, while 32.8 metric tonnes were recorded in 2025, bringing the cumulative volume for the two years to 223.699 metric tonnes. “The summary is that a total of 190.8 metric tonnes of LPG was exported in 2024. A total of 32.8 metric tonnes was exported in 2025, and the cumulative volume of LPG exports recorded for the two-year period stood at 223.699 metric tonnes,” she said. She disclosed that the Customs Service had no record of LPG exports at Escravos in 2026. According to her, LPG exports require clearance certificates from the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, while exporters must also make declarations through the agency’s automated system. “For the 2026 export of LPG at Escravos, our system showed no records of export because, for you to make an export, there must be an export clearance certificate sent to us by the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, which we send to the commands, and the exporter must make a declaration on our system, which is automated,” she said. She added that approved LPG export volumes stood at 400 metric tonnes for the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited and 386.4 metric tonnes for Chevron. Also speaking, a representative of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, Enorense Amadasu, said the offshore facility was originally designed to accommodate the evacuation of LPG for export. He explained that the facility operates under a joint venture involving the Federal Government, represented by the NNPC, and Chevron, with the parties having existing export arrangements. Amadasu said the commission had engaged the operator to explore the possibility of redirecting some of the LPG to the domestic market. He disclosed that Chevron issued a public request in 2024 inviting Nigerian LPG off-takers to discuss possible arrangements for supplying the local market. “Having said that, when we got this request, we decided to engage the operator to get more details, and that was when we were made to understand that Chevron had actually put out a public request sometime in 2024, to request for Nigeria LPG off-takers to come for them to discuss the possibility of working with some of them to see how they can work it to change some of this to the domestic market,” he said. In his remarks, Senator Aniekan Bassey (APC, Akwa Ibom North-East), a member of the committee, said the hearing provided an opportunity for lawmakers to examine issues affecting the oil and gas industry, particularly accountability, regulation and the management of petroleum resources. Bassey reaffirmed his commitment to supporting legislative interventions aimed at promoting transparency, strengthening institutional accountability and advancing Nigeria’s economic interests. The committee is expected to continue its engagement with relevant stakeholders next Tuesday as it seeks to address domestic LPG supply gaps, improve export revenue remittances and ensure increased availability of cooking gas in the country. items.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi on Nov 27
items.description: A local holiday has been declared in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi for Nov 27 (Friday). A notification issued by the Islamabad deputy commissioner stated that Nov 27 “has been declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of ICT”. It noted that all essential services would remain operational during the holiday, including the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority, the ICT administration, Islamabad police, the Islamabad Electric Supply Company, the Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited and hospitals. Separately, the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner shared a notification on X stating that a local holiday had been declared in the district for Nov 27. He said that all schools, colleges and offices would remain closed. The notification said that all “emergency dealing departments/institutions/authorities shall remain operational”. “Moreover, all annual and supplementary examinations shall be conducted as per the approved schedule in all education institutes of Rawalpindi district,” it said. Both notifications did not provide a reason for the holiday. The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) also issued a notification ordering that no judicial work be conducted on Friday at the principal seat of the court in Islamabad, on account of the closure of the city’s Red Zone and the consequent difficulties expected to be faced by lawyers, litigants and officials of the court in reaching the premises. “The cause list of the court shall stand cancelled. However, all officers and staff shall work from home and shall not leave the station,” the notification said. It added that the four branch registries of the court would all remain open for judicial and administrative work. Meanwhile, a notice of expected partial closure was issued for the Rawalpindi-Islamabad metro system from Nov 26-28, as a result of expected “VIP movement”. The notice warned of a possible suspension of the line from Kashmir Highway to the Pak Secretariat stations and said the closure of the last four stops was also under consideration. The metro service from Saddar to Faiz Ahmed Faiz would remain operational, it added.

items.title: Nasarawa 2027: Adamu pledges to construct Ekye-Doma road, vows to tackle insecurity
items.description: The Nasarawa State governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party, retired Inspector-General of Police Mohammed Adamu, has promised to prioritise the construction of the Ekye-Doma road if elected, saying its poor condition is worsening insecurity and hampering farming activities. Adamu said the road had been neglected for years despite the incumbent administration spending nearly eight years in office, adding that its rehabilitation would improve transportation, support farmers and help tackle insecurity in the area. He spoke on Wednesday during an engagement with residents of Ekye Development Area in Doma Local Government Area, where he said the visit was aimed at listening to their concerns and presenting his plans for the state. The former police chief said the road was a major concern raised by residents, traditional rulers and people from the area living in Abuja, noting that its condition had become a hindrance to economic activities and security. “Insha Allah, if elected, the first road we will construct is this one,” Adamu said, pledging to address the challenges confronting the community. He added, “This is one of the major factors contributing to insecurity in this region. Our administration will put an end to this menace and bring succour to the people.” Adamu accused the incumbent government of neglecting the area, arguing that the failure to improve the road reflected a disconnect between the government and the people. “There are several indications that the incumbent government has abandoned the people. First, this road has been neglected for many years. This government has spent almost eight years in office but has not even graded the road,” he said. The SDP candidate also promised free education from primary to secondary school and free treatment for common illnesses, including malaria, typhoid, diabetes and hypertension, if elected. He said the proposed interventions were designed to reduce the financial pressure on households and improve residents’ living conditions. “Government is about the people. Without the people, government loses its meaning and purpose,” Adamu said, adding that anyone seeking public office must prioritise the welfare of citizens. He said he and his team had decided to leave their comfort zones to contest for leadership because of the hardship facing residents, expressing confidence that they could address the state’s challenges through policies aimed at improving socioeconomic conditions. items.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place. Bilawal made the remarks while speaking at another “Meet the Press” event, this time at the Multan Press Club. The Bhutto scion is on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, making stops in Multan , Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh so far. Responding to a query about him calling former premier Imran Khan a “political prisoner”, Bilawal explained that he made the “controversial” statement in a polarised political environment, where those terming him a political prisoner could not be convinced otherwise and those declaring him a convict and corrupt could not be convinced otherwise. Bilawal stressed that in his speech, not the press queries, he made an observation that was not about Imran, but rather about Pakistan’s political history wherein elected premiers often end up going to jail later on or come to power after being imprisoned. “Whatever opinion you may hold about Khan sahib , even if you think he is not a political prisoner, there is no denying the fact that PTI is a political reality,” the PPP chairman stressed. He emphasised that even if Imran was considered a “convicted felon or terrorist or whatever”, prisoners in a respectable society were entitled to their rights. Bilawal said that although the PTI founder “tried to deny my family those rights”, he would not want to continue the cycle of “repeating the same mistakes” in vengeance. “Khan sahib is a convict, he is in jail, but PTI is a political reality. Until PTI’s trust is restored in this system […] and they are able to play their role in the Parliament, the reset that is being discussed cannot take place in that manner,” he maintained. The PPP chairman’s latest remarks come amid a growing debate over a “system reset” in the country. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units , arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”. In a similar vein, the Bhutto scion on Monday had called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system. During Thursday’s address, Bilawal reiterated his call to regain the opposition’s “lost trust” in the system and for the government to undertake confidence-building measures (CBMs) to convince it that institutions such as the Parliament, the Election Commission of Pakistan, the courts, and the accountability system could be trusted again. Responding to a query, Bilawal reiterated that the disputed reserved seats of the 2024 elections were a “low-hanging fruit” through which the opposition’s trust could be restored and that could serve as a CBM. The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol. “Political parties will have to negotiate among themselves, or approach the court, or carry out reforms, so this gets done,” Bilawal suggested, adding that he was “not happy that another party” does not have its electoral symbol today. “Personally, I believe they (PTI) should have received the reserved seats,” said Bilawal, whose PPP was one of the parties to challenge the Supreme Court ruling that declared PTI eligible for those seats. However, in a deviation from that, Bilawal today said, “When PTI itself is saying that I am PTI, then we should listen to what they say and acknowledge it. However, that did not happen .” Referring to the SC Constitutional Bench’s 2025 order that overturned the July 2024 ruling and consequently handed the seats to the coalition parties, Bilawal said, “That order, in my opinion, was also slightly extra.” He said that even if his stance was that PTI should not get the reserved seats based on the argument that their leaders did not contest as PTI candidates, “how can those seats be given to me or the PML-N or JUI?” Bilawal added: “According to that very argument, the argument on which you say that PTI cannot get [reserved seats] because they are not PTI, they are SIC, then I am not PTI either, JUI is not PTI, PML-N is not PTI.” The PPP chairman stressed he was only raising this point because he believed if the opposition’s trust is to be restored, the government will have to think about such “goodwill gestures”. ‘All decisions have to be made in Parliament alone’ At the same time, the PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part and urged the opposition to view its role as a responsibility rather than a choice. “They should sit in our finance committee in the Parliament. When the government presents the budget, [they should give their] input,” he said, adding that the opposition’s role was essential to tackling unemployment, inflation and poverty. “But they haven’t been doing it for quite some time. They come for the judiciary, but there is also a committee for the judiciary, they do not sit in that either. They are not present in all committees of the Parliament,” Bilawal pointed out. He called on the opposition to review if they benefitted from their boycott of such parliamentary initiatives, urging that it take part in the recently proposed electoral reforms committee . “Until there are free and fair elections, until our country, our nation, all provinces, and all parties have confidence in this electoral system, there will be no trust, and the governments formed or referendums held as a result of that electoral system will lack legitimacy and strength,” Bilawal asserted. The PPP chairman reiterated his stance that any “reset or reboot of our system” should be democratic and political, with all political stakeholders, including the opposition, made part of the conversation. “If we want to make the Parliament functional, then all decisions have to be made in the Parliament alone,” he said, adding that decisions taken “outside the Parliament” would leave the system incapable of overcoming challenges. Regarding a proposed “reset” in the country, Bilawal said even though he had not started the conversation, the discussion was welcomed. “This country’s system has collapsed. I believe we should take this conversation forward: if the system has collapsed, why is that? How did it happen? Did it happen on its own? Because of political workers? Because of political parties?” he questioned. “If you do not want to determine the responsibility for it, then don’t. But if you’re sick and I need to get you treated, then first I have to diagnose you to figure out what the illness is.” He stressed that unless the stakeholders together identified why the system collapsed, there would be difficulties reviving it. Recalling his Nov 17 remarks, Bilawal said the “system, meaning the 1973 Constitution, did not collapse on its own, it was made to collapse again and again”. The PPP chairman called for a debate to identify the “diagnosis” with consensus, adding that a “reset should not be decided by a few former and current media anchors, media owners, and a few people belonging to business sectors, as they would not draw attention to people’s real issues”. At one point, Bilawal remarked that nationalist parties in Sindh label PPP as “ wafaaqparast” (pro-Centre) and those in Islamabad “affectionately call us “ qoumparast ” (nationalist), but his party was “ Pakistan-parast and awaamparast ”. ‘You can’t have a hard state with thin skin’ The Bhutto scion further said, “This country should have enough courage that we can listen to the truth and tolerate each other’s differences of opinion.” He termed the reactions to his Nov 17 press conference as “inappropriate”, contending that there were patriotic Pakistanis on both sides of an argument even if they had differing opinions. Bilawal continued: “If anyone thinks that we can be silenced through such cheap tactics, that is not possible. “It is now said these days that ‘Pakistan is a hard state’. For Pakistan to be that, the hard state should have thick skin. You can’t have a hard state with thin skin.” Responding to a question, Bilawal said he not only condemned the recent actions against the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief during his stay in Lahore, but also termed them “incomprehensible”. “If you will take such revengeful actions even against Maulana Fazlur Rehman, then do you expect them to clap for you or praise you?” he remarked. The PPP chairman argued that as an opposition member, it was Fazl’s “patriotic duty” to criticise the government. “We should have a thick skin and absorb that criticism,” he said, adding that any suggestion in it that could lead to better decisions should be incorporated. ‘Non-existent press freedom’ During his address, the PPP chairman also highlighted the importance of a free press, adding that he wanted to restore the “power” previously held by press clubs across the country. “With your voice, your columns, you used to make and topple governments,” the Bhutto scion remarked. “I don’t want to topple any government, nor do I want to form another one. But I believe your role is to hold up a mirror to those sitting in power,” he added. Bilawal said he was not denying “mistakes” made by him over time, insisting that his party’s intention was not to weaken the press. He referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), which was amended in January 2025 despite countrywide protests by journalists’ bodies. He remarked that regardless of the PPP’s intention, the country had now arrived at a point where press freedom was non-existent. The PPP chairman noted that if the media was given space only to regurgitate what those in power talked about among themselves, then issues related to economic crises and difficulties faced by the people at the grassroots level would not come to the forefront. ‘27th Amendment a success but judicial system lacks trust’ Bilawal also elaborated on his earlier remarks about the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, insisting that an impression was being given as if he was backing away from them or criticising them. In his Nov 17 remark, the PPP chairman, who had strongly advocated for the amendments at the time of their passage, had said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor bilateral agreement; it was passed with brute majority”. He had also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation. The next day, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution. “It’s not black and white,” Bilawal said today, stressing that the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment were passed through mutual consensus. He defended that the 26th Amendment was passed with as much consensus as could be developed and declared the passage of the 27th Amendment with a two-thirds majority a “success”. “But, at the same time, I believe we cannot ignore the fact today that our opposition does not have confidence in this judicial system,” Bilawal stated, adding that judges and lawyers he interacts with are also “not comfortable” with the current status of the judiciary. “Does this mean I am saying we should tear it up? No. I am merely asking what steps we can take, how can dialogue be held with all stakeholders, so that we can restore that lost trust?” The PPP chairman clarified that while an attempt was made to make his “brute majority” remarks on the 27th Amendment controversial, as if he had meant force or used the word “brutal”, he had simply referred to the two-thirds majority that the legislation had. ‘Accountability system used solely for political opponents’ During his address, the PPP chairman also doubled down on his criticism of the country’s accountability system, asserting that its structure was “based on political victimisation” “Unfortunately, no matter how big the claims the governments came in with, the more emphasis they placed on eradicating corruption, the more corruption there has been,” he remarked. Bilawal contended that despite strong rhetoric by governments on ending corruption, they failed to do so as the accountability system was “used solely against political opponents”. The PPP chairman regretted that ongoing discussions in the Parliament, the federal cabinet, seminars, or even television talk shows did not pay attention to the fundamental issues faced by the public. “People are distressed about managing two square meals. They’re worried whether they should educate their children or arrange medicines for their elders,” he said. Bilawal noted there was “restlessness and distress” among Pakistan’s youth, who faced unemployment and, even if employed, their salaries were spent on just commuting to and from work. “If we truly want this system to serve the public, want our country to be capable of facing every problem, whether they are economic hardships or foreign difficulties, then we will have to take steps as soon as possible so we can establish unity, political stability, and restore trust in all institutions,” he stated.

items.title: FG urges South Korean firms to establish factories
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has urged major South Korean companies to establish manufacturing and assembly plants in Nigeria as part of efforts to create jobs, boost local production and strengthen the country’s industrial capacity. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, made the appeal when South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yo-an, visited him in Abuja on Tuesday. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. Enikanolaiye said the presence of South Korean brands, including LG, Kia and Samsung, in Nigeria reflected the growing trade relations between both countries. He urged the companies to build on the existing relationship by establishing factories and operational offices in Nigeria, citing the country’s young and skilled workforce. The minister also called for increased South Korean investment in agriculture, solid minerals, manufacturing and the marine economy. In his response, Jeong identified technology transfer, industrial development and agriculture as areas with significant potential for closer cooperation between the two countries. He said South Korea was ready to share its development experience with Nigeria to support the country’s industrial growth. The two sides also discussed plans to hold the seventh session of the Nigeria–Korea Joint Commission in the first quarter of 2027. They further emphasised the need to conclude outstanding bilateral agreements, including an agreement on the avoidance of double taxation. The post FG urges South Korean firms to establish factories appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘I have no time for anybody’ – Okpebholo denies involvement in NDC Edo attack
items.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has dismissed allegations linking him to the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin City, saying he has no time for those accusing him. Okpebholo spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ehor, the administrative headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, a day after gunmen attacked NDC supporters who had gathered along Airport Road to welcome the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state. The governor described the allegations against him as lies, insisting that he did not use thugs during his previous political campaigns. “Yesterday some people were crying because when they thought they would come to Edo and shine, when they got here, they met only three people in the hall. They started shooting themselves because they want to spoil our name. They started calling my name but I have no time for anybody. They are lying,” he said. He added that hearing his name mentioned during a television report made him conclude that the claims being circulated about him were untrue. Okpebholo also denied using thugs during his political campaigns, recalling his contests for the Senate and governorship. “When I was contesting for Senate, I didn’t use thugs. When I was contesting for governor, I did not use thugs,” he said. The governor further claimed that the NDC chairman was among those previously implicated in the killing of his police officer, but said he had refrained from pursuing the matter to avoid accusations of political victimisation. “The NDC chairman was one of those that were fingered at that time. If I start now, they will say that I am victimising them because of politics,” he added. The attack occurred on Wednesday along Airport Road in Benin City, where gunmen reportedly opened fire on people waiting to receive Obi ahead of his town hall meeting in the state. The Edo State Police Command said three gunmen in a black Toyota Hilux opened fire after encountering police operatives stationed at the airport exit gate. One person, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was taken to hospital. The police said Commissioner of Police Patrick Daaor had ordered an investigation and directed tactical operatives to track down the fleeing suspects. The NDC condemned the incident and called for an investigation into the attack. As of Thursday, the police had not publicly identified the suspects or announced any arrests. The post ‘I have no time for anybody’ – Okpebholo denies involvement in NDC Edo attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca termine sur une note stable
items.description: Le MASI, indice phare de la Bourse de Casablanca, a clôturé la séance de jeudi sur une note stable, à 16.570,52 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a progressé de 0,31% à 1.240,08 pts, alors que le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,53% à 1.241,18 pts. De son côté, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a gagné 0,27% à 1.570,98 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Services de transport » (+3,57%), « Boissons » (+2,28%) et « Industrie pharmaceutique » (+1,69%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Mines » (-2,47%), « Électricité » (-1,68%) et « Transport » (-1,13%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. Les échanges ont avoisiné 136 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central et dominés par les transactions sur Laprophan (27,77 MDH), Attijariwafa bank (22,56 MDH) et Managem (11,56 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 965 milliards de dirhams (MMDH). Aux valeurs individuelles, Auto Nejma (+5,98% à 6.041 DH), Sodep Marsa Maroc (+3,57% à 779,9 DH), Laprophan (+3,33% à 310 DH), Minière Touissit (+3,06% à 3.130 DH) et Société des Boissons du Maroc (+2,98% à 1.968 DH) ont affiché les plus fortes progressions. À l'opposé, BMCI (-3,53% à 548,9 DH), Managem (-3,2% à 1.151 DH), Disty Technologies (-2,73% à 338,5 DH), Colorado (-2,7% à 72 DH) et Afma (-2,36% à 1.240 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. The post La Bourse de Casablanca termine sur une note stable appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Two injured in police clash with residents at Twifo Praso; station vandalised
items.description: Two men have sustained gunshot wounds following a violent confrontation between police and residents of Twifo Praso in the Central Region, which also resulted in the vandalisation of the local police station. The injured men were taken to the Praso Government Hospital, where they are receiving medical treatment. The violence broke out early Thursday during an operation by the Police Intelligence Directorate (PID) of the Central North Regional Police Command to dismantle makeshift structures, popularly known as “ghettos,” near the Pra River, suspected to be centres for illicit drug activities. The raid forms part of an ongoing regional crackdown on drug trafficking and consumption, which has reportedly resulted in several arrests and prosecutions. However, the operation was met with resistance from some youths who confronted and attacked the officers, leading to an escalation of tensions. Police reportedly fired warning shots to disperse the crowd, but two young men, who were allegedly attempting to set a police pickup vehicle on fire during the confrontation, were hit by bullets. The incident triggered further unrest, with an angry group of residents subsequently storming the Twifo Praso Police Station to demand that officers involved in the operation be handed over to them. During the attack, several glass windows at the police station were smashed, while an unconfirmed number of police officers reportedly sustained injuries. Security reinforcements have since been deployed to the area to contain the situation and prevent further violence. A team from the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has also joined security personnel in efforts to restore calm in the town.

items.title: Delta attack: PANDEF writes IGP, DSS DG, demands probe
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has written to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, demanding an urgent investigation into the reported violence at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The socio-political organisation called on both security chiefs to work with other relevant agencies to identify and prosecute those who allegedly planned, sponsored, instigated or participated in the attack on the campaign train of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Omo-Agege, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, was reportedly attacked during a campaign rally on Monday, November 23, 2026, with some persons said to have been killed and several others injured. In a letter signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, PANDEF strongly condemned the incident and described the reported loss of lives and injuries as disturbing and unacceptable. The organisation also urged the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide financial and other forms of assistance to families of those reportedly killed, as well as adequate medical care for the injured. In the letter, PANDEF said it was shocked by reports of violence at a political rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in parts of Uduere, Delta State, on Monday. It, however, noted that the reports of deaths and injuries had yet to be officially corroborated. “According to media reports, which are yet to be officially corroborated, some persons reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. We consider these reported incidents extremely disturbing and totally unacceptable,” the letter stated. PANDEF recalled that it had issued a statement the previous week warning against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South. It said the latest incident, coming days after its appeal, was a source of grave concern, adding that the region had traditionally upheld political tolerance, sportsmanship and civility. The organisation further warned that insecurity in the South-South could have implications beyond the region, given its strategic importance to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry and national economy. “Any disruption of peace and security in the region, particularly violence associated with political and electoral activities, could have far-reaching implications, not only for the safety and wellbeing of our people but also for the stability and economic survival of the country,” it said. PANDEF urged the police, DSS and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice in accordance with the law. It also reiterated that political competition must not degenerate into violence, intimidation or the unlawful taking of human lives. The organisation called on political actors and their supporters to uphold tolerance, respect opposing views and embrace peaceful participation in the democratic process. items.title: ‘What has changed in the pockets of Ghanaians?’ – Afenyo-Markin challenges government
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has questioned the impact of the government’s reported economic gains on ordinary Ghanaians, arguing that official statistics do not reflect the financial realities facing households and businesses. He described what he called a divide between the “paper economy” presented by the government and the “pocket economy” experienced by citizens. Contributing to the closing debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, 2026, Afenyo-Markin said the two economies were increasingly disconnected. “One lives in speeches as presented by the Finance Minister, social media posts as advanced by the government communications minister, lovely presentations and settings for only NDC government functionaries and party communicators belong to this first arm of the economy. Then the real one lives in the kitchen, the classroom, the market, and the struggling entrepreneurs and the people of Ghana,” he stated. Afenyo-Markin argued that improvements in economic indicators would have little meaning to citizens if they did not translate into lower living costs and better financial conditions. “The market woman cannot eat paper. The student cannot pay school fees with a government statement. The parent counting coins at the end of the month cannot feed a child with a number,” he said. He questioned whether the reported decline in prices and improvements in economic indicators were making a meaningful difference to households and small businesses. “So I ask again, what has changed in the pocket of Ghanaians? If prices come down on paper, but not at the market, who has been helped? If the numbers go up but the small business owner is still closing a shop, who has been saved?” he added. The government has highlighted improvements in key macroeconomic indicators, including declining inflation and relative stability in the exchange rate, as evidence of progress in its economic management. The Minority, however, has repeatedly argued that these gains are not translating into sufficient relief for ordinary Ghanaians, particularly households and small businesses facing high living costs. The debate on the 2027 Budget is expected to conclude with a vote in Parliament.

items.title: 2027 Polls: We’re working with security agencies to prosecute offenders – INEC
items.description: …Moneybags hijacking our elections, ex-NBA president Osigwe laments By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) said on Thursday that it is working closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, spoke at the opening session of the 2026 Annual Conference of the National Association of Judiciary Correspondents (NAJUC). He said the Commission would initiate action against identified offenders upon receipt of investigative case files from the relevant security agencies. According to Amupitan, the collaboration is based on a decentralised framework known as ICCES Tentacles, which is also aimed at curbing campaign impunity. He added that the prosecutions would be guided by the Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties 2026 and the enhanced deterrence provisions of Sections 95, 96, 97 and 148 of the Electoral Act 2026. In a goodwill message presented by his Chief Press Secretary (CPS), Mr. Adedayo Oketola, the INEC Chairman said the theme of the conference, “Deepening Nigeria’s Electoral Integrity: The Ballot Versus The Verdict,” captured one of the most consequential questions in the nation’s constitutional democracy. He insisted that the integrity of Nigeria’s democratic process depends on seamless institutional synergy between those who conduct elections and those who adjudicate electoral disputes. “When the polling unit produces credible records and the tribunal applies the law with dispatch and consistency, public trust in both the ballot and the verdict is reinforced. “Public confidence in democracy erodes whenever citizens perceive that elections are won in the courtroom rather than at the polling unit—or, conversely, when judicial processes are weaponised through frivolous pre-election and post-election litigation. “Equally damaging is the distortion of judicial pronouncements in public discourse, where nuanced rulings are stripped of legal context and weaponised to inflame political tension. “Strengthening electoral jurisprudence therefore requires shared discipline across all actors. “We need an electoral commission that conducts transparent, verifiable polls; political parties that respect internal democracy and the rule of law; courts that dispense predictable, substantial justice; and a judiciary press corps committed to precision and fairness. “For INEC, the best way to ease the litigation burden on our courts ahead of the Presidential and National Assembly elections on Saturday, 16th January 2027, and the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls on Saturday, 6th February 2027—starting with our nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise this Saturday, 28th November 2026—is to eliminate administrative ambiguity at the source. “Guided by the Electoral Act 2026 and lessons drawn from recent off-cycle elections, the Commission has anchored its preparation on four evidentiary and operational safeguards,” he added. Meanwhile, in his presentation, the immediate past President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Mr. Afam Osigwe, SAN, who was the lead speaker at the conference, said he was worried that moneybags were hijacking elections in the country. “The type of electoral process we have is making it difficult for honest persons to contest elections. Moneybags are hijacking the elections. “Wrong persons who have no business seeking leadership positions are the ones fighting for elective offices, and it should not be that way,” Osigwe stated. He argued that courts should not be involved in determining who represents a political party at an election. “If a political party chooses to field a villain as their candidate for a constituency, the voters should decide. “But because people know that their votes would not count, they want the courts to take decisions for them, and in Nigeria today, people are not only forum shopping; they are also judge shopping. “They are shopping for judges to determine cases. The truth must be told,” the former NBA President added, even as he accused the courts of becoming too technical. Attributing growing voter apathy to the perception that votes do not count, Osigwe argued that where the votes counted and announced fail to reflect the will of the people, it exposes a fundamental weakness in the system. He warned that the day Nigerians completely lose interest in democracy, the country may face consequences it will not be comfortable with. The NBA President, Mrs. Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, SAN, who was represented by Dr. Prince Azubuike, said electoral credibility depends not only on free, fair and transparent elections but also on the integrity of the judicial processes through which disputes are determined. She said the judiciary must remain independent and impartial, with decisions grounded in law, supported by sound reasoning and delivered without fear or favour. While the keynote speaker, Dr. Sam Amadi, lamented what he described as the recurring lack of coherence in judicial decisions and the absence of jurisprudential guidance for judges, the media aide to the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Mr. Tobi Soniyi, urged political parties to learn to resolve their disputes internally without unnecessary recourse to the courts. Mr. Soniyi argued that many cases suffer delays owing to the volume of political matters that saturate court dockets. Earlier, in his welcome address, the Chairman of NAJUC, Abuja Chapter, Mr. Olakunle Olasanmi, noted that although the country had recorded improvements in voter registration technology, biometric verification and transparency in the transmission of results, persistent challenges such as logistical failures, voter intimidation, violence and delayed results continued to undermine public confidence. Olasanmi warned that allowing politicians who perpetrate electoral violence and manipulate the process to secure favourable judgments could encourage the continuation of such practices, particularly where perpetrators believe they can ultimately retain political power through litigation. The post 2027 Polls: We’re working with security agencies to prosecute offenders – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Après l’inauguration du siège de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso et de deux Espaces numériques ouverts (ENO), le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a poursuivi, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, la série d’inaugurations avec celle des nouvelles infrastructures de l’École polytechnique de Ouagadougou (EPO), situées dans le quartier de Nagrin. Ces réalisations renforcent les capacités d’accueil et les moyens de formation pratique de l’établissement. ‎ ‎ Quatre infrastructures ont été inaugurées : un bâtiment pédagogique de type R+3, réalisé pour un coût de 1 317 463 757 FCFA TTC, comprenant des salles de cours, des bureaux administratifs et des espaces de réunion, pour une capacité totale de 2 000 places assises ; un bâtiment abritant 14 laboratoires de travaux pratiques et une salle multimédia, réalisé pour 587 millions de FCFA TTC ; un atelier de génie mécanique, d’un coût de 150 millions de FCFA TTC ; et un atelier de génie textile, d’une valeur de 57 millions de FCFA TTC, partiellement équipé pour la filature, le tissage et le tricotage. ‎ ‎ Pour le ministre chargé de l’Enseignement supérieur, le Pr Ardjouma Thiombiano, cette inauguration marque une étape importante dans le développement de l’EPO. Depuis sa création, l’établissement fonctionnait dans des bâtiments loués, pour une charge d’environ 12 millions de FCFA par mois. Selon le ministre, ces nouvelles infrastructures permettront à l’État de mettre fin à cette dépense récurrente tout en offrant à l’école un cadre de formation adapté à ses ambitions. ‎ ‎ L’École polytechnique de Ouagadougou compte environ 659 élèves ingénieurs inscrits et forme des cadres dans plusieurs domaines, notamment les technologies et l’informatique. Depuis sa création, elle a contribué à la formation et à l’insertion de près de 104 ingénieurs dans le tissu socio-économique national. Le ministre a également annoncé une prochaine phase de développement de l’EPO, conformément aux orientations du Chef de l’État. ‎ ‎ À travers ces réalisations, le Gouvernement réaffirme son engagement en faveur d’un enseignement supérieur axé sur la formation pratique et le développement des compétences scientifiques et technologiques de la jeunesse burkinabè. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to the President on Media and Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said President Bola Tinubu is willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists, while maintaining that the Presidency will decide which media organisations interview him. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. And the President, when granting interviews, didn’t need to read anything, didn’t need to be briefed,” he said. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. We decide who we grant interviews to. Nobody can come and tell us, grant to this one and not the other one,” he said. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. So every day, the activity of the President is covered by them,” Bwala said. He also criticised some media practitioners over what he described as political bias and a lack of professionalism, arguing that Tinubu should engage journalists capable of conducting balanced interviews. Bwala’s remarks followed criticism of Tinubu’s recent interview with American political strategist and media personality Diana London. Some Nigerians questioned why the President had granted an interview to a foreign media personality while rarely speaking with Nigerian journalists. The controversy grew after reports linked London to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving a United States-based firm engaged by the Nigerian government. London denied receiving the money from the Federal Government or anyone in Nigeria, saying she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also challenged Tinubu to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists and called for the release of the full, unedited recording of his conversation with London. He questioned whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying arrangement. Bwala also reiterated that the President should do more interviews with local journalists, saying, “I expect us to do more.” The post Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: Le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a procédé, ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à l’inauguration du siège de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso (UV-BF) et de deux Espaces numériques ouverts (ENO), situés à Bonheur-Ville et à Tampouy. Ces infrastructures s’inscrivent dans la dynamique de transformation du secteur éducatif impulsée par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, avec pour ambition d’offrir à la jeunesse des conditions de formation adaptées aux exigences du monde contemporain. ‎ ‎ Le siège de l’UV-BF est constitué d’un bâtiment de type R+4 avec sous-sol, complété par un plateau omnisports et des ouvrages communautaires. L’ensemble a nécessité un investissement de 6,9 milliards de francs CFA. Le bâtiment abrite notamment sept salles de réunion équipées pour la visioconférence, une salle polyvalente, 71 bureaux, un laboratoire de réalité virtuelle, un studio de production audiovisuelle, un mini-centre de données, une salle de monitoring et 28 locaux techniques. ‎ ‎ Les ENO de Tampouy et de Bonheur-Ville, qui constituent des relais de proximité, ont nécessité un investissement de 3,2 milliards de francs CFA chacun. Chaque complexe comprend notamment un amphithéâtre pouvant accueillir jusqu’à 300 personnes, deux espaces de travail ouverts, une salle de formation, des bureaux et plusieurs locaux techniques. ‎ ‎ Le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo Pour le Premier ministre, ces réalisations traduisent la volonté affirmée des autorités de faire de la formation du capital humain une priorité nationale. « Ce sont des investissements inédits qui permettent aujourd’hui de moderniser l’offre d’enseignement, d’accroître les capacités d’accueil et surtout de consolider et d’affirmer davantage la place centrale accordée à la formation de la jeunesse dans la Révolution progressiste populaire », a-t-il souligné. ‎ ‎ Le Camarade ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Pr. Ardjouma Thiombiano Au-delà de leur dimension infrastructurelle, ces réalisations constituent une réponse concrète aux défis liés à l’accessibilité géographique et sociale de l’enseignement supérieur. Elles offrent aux étudiants de meilleures conditions de formation et contribuent à réduire les disparités entre les apprenants des grandes villes et ceux des localités éloignées. ‎ ‎ Le président de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso, Oumarou Zalé, exprimant sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour leur accompagnement. Dans son intervention, le Camarade ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Pr. Ardjouma Thiombiano, a expliqué que ce dispositif vise à garantir une formation accessible à tous, sans distinction de lieu de résidence ou de condition sociale. « L’objectif est de faire en sorte qu’aucun étudiant, aucun enfant du Burkina Faso ne soit exclu de la formation en raison de l’éloignement géographique ou de difficultés sociales », a-t-il indiqué. ‎ ‎ Le ministre a également mis en avant les possibilités qu’offre l’enseignement à distance pour mobiliser les compétences. Outre les enseignants intervenant depuis le siège de l’Université, le dispositif permet de solliciter des enseignants-chercheurs d’autres institutions, notamment ceux de la diaspora et des universités étrangères. ‎ ‎ Au nom des étudiants, le Camarade Tindegma Zongo a salué la réalisation de ces infrastructures, qui apportent des réponses à plusieurs difficultés rencontrées par les apprenants inscrits dans les formations à distance. Il a notamment évoqué les contraintes liées à l’accès aux équipements informatiques, à la connexion Internet et à l’accompagnement pédagogique. ‎ ‎« Désormais, l’Université virtuelle a un visage et des lieux où se retrouver », s’est-il réjoui. Au nom de ses camarades, il a pris l’engagement de contribuer à la préservation de ces infrastructures par la discipline, la responsabilité et la recherche de l’excellence. ‎ ‎ Pour sa part, le président de l’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso, Oumarou Zalé, a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux plus hautes autorités du pays pour leur accompagnement dans la concrétisation de ces projets. Il a souligné que ces réalisations constituent un tournant important dans le développement de l’institution. Elles lui permettront de disposer d’un cadre de travail approprié pour renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles et améliorer l’accompagnement des étudiants. ‎ ‎ L’Université virtuelle du Burkina Faso a pour mission de promouvoir un enseignement supérieur performant et compétitif, fondé sur les technologies de l’information et de la communication ainsi que sur l’enseignement à distance. Son siège constitue le centre de pilotage où sont conçus et produits les contenus pédagogiques destinés aux étudiants de l’ensemble du territoire national. Les ENO servent de relais de proximité. ‎ ‎ D’autres infrastructures sont annoncées dans les prochaines semaines, notamment à Bobo-Dioulasso, Koudougou, Fada N’Gourma et Ziniaré. À terme, l’ambition est de doter chaque région du Burkina Faso d’au moins un Espace numérique ouvert, afin de rapprocher l’offre de formation des populations et de renforcer l’équité territoriale. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: Police arrest 7 Asafo group members over Akwambo festival clash at Gomoa Nyanyano
items.description: The Central East Regional Police Command has arrested seven members of the Asafo group at Gomoa Nyanyano in the Gomoa East District following tensions over the celebration of the Akwambo festival amid a protracted chieftaincy dispute. The suspects are Sarfohene Kwesi; Saah, leader of the Asafo No. 1 group; Kwabena Baidoo; Joshua Embreye; Okeyerema Kofi Ackom, chief drummer for Asafo No. 2; Kweku Egyiri, a member of Asafo No. 2; and Kofi Awotwe, also a member of the Asafo group. The arrests were made on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, after the group allegedly proceeded with the festival despite an injunction issued by the Judicial Committee of the Gomoa Assin Traditional Council restraining parties from engaging in traditional activities in the area. Read also: VIDEO: Gunshots heighten tension at Nyanyano over chieftaincy dispute Addressing a press conference on Thursday, Central East Regional Police Commander, DCOP Francis Nchor, said the group had initially approached the police seeking permission to organise a two-week homecoming celebration. However, police investigations revealed that the proposed event was intended to be an Akwambo festival. He said the police subsequently invited the group’s leaders, informed them of their findings and advised them against proceeding with activities that could undermine peace in the community. Despite the warning, police received information at about 4:30 p.m. on Wednesday that members of the group had begun the celebration. Officers who proceeded to the scene found some members drumming and dancing along the principal street of Gomoa Nyanyano, leading to the arrest of seven suspects. DCOP Nchor said shortly after the arrests, some youth in the community besieged the Gomoa Nyanyano Police Station and pelted officers with stones and other offensive weapons. Read also: Calm returns to Nyanyano after gunshots; police deploy 50 officers The incident resulted in damage to parts of a stationary police service vehicle. The crowd was subsequently dispersed, while the Command says the security situation is currently under control. Police have intensified patrols in the community and say the seven suspects will be arraigned before court. The Command has urged residents to remain calm, cooperate with security personnel and respect the injunction issued by the traditional council.

items.title: Tinubu approves free trade zone, two flyovers for Anambra
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of a Free Trade Zone for the proposed Anambra Industrial City, alongside the construction of two flyovers in Awka, as part of efforts to boost industrialisation and infrastructure development in the South-East. Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced the approvals on Thursday during the commissioning of the Ekwulobia flyover in Aguata Local Government Area of Anambra State. He said the Free Trade Zone would provide investors with tax incentives and other benefits, encouraging the establishment of factories, export-oriented businesses and employment opportunities. “It means emergence of factories, export of products, new jobs. It means that one day, products manufactured in Anambra will be sold outside the state and beyond,” Shettima said. According to him, the President also approved flyovers at Regina Caeli Junction and the Nnamdi Azikiwe University gate, both in Awka. He listed other federal government-approved projects to include the dualisation of the 150-kilometre Oba-Nnewi-Uga-Ihube Road and the 108-kilometre Otuocha-Anam-Abaji Road, which he said would reduce the journey between Awka and Abuja to less than five hours. Shettima also disclosed that the Federal Government was constructing a 35-kilometre ring road with seven bridges to link the Second Niger Bridge and ease traffic congestion around Onitsha. He said the government was also committing about N350 billion to the reconstruction of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway. The Vice-President said the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), established by the Tinubu administration, had received a provision of N140 billion in the 2026 budget to drive economic development in the region. He said the commission was expected to help grow the region’s economy to $200 billion within the next 10 years. “I share all these to show that development has no political party. The Federal Government is always a willing partner and we are happy that Governor Soludo is delivering for his people,” he said. Shettima commended Governor Chukwuma Soludo for infrastructure development and urban renewal, citing the transformation of Okpoko and the completion of the Ekwulobia flyover. He urged residents to support the state government by paying their taxes and levies, saying the revenue would be channelled into public services, including healthcare and education. He added that sustainable infrastructure development required continuity, urging Nigerians to support ongoing projects rather than abandon them for new ones. “Good roads are not built in one season; great cities are not built in one term. The works of Renewed Hope in Anambra and across Nigeria need steady hands to finish,” he said. The Vice-President also praised Soludo and his party, the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), for their political cooperation with President Tinubu, saying the partnership was already yielding benefits. Describing Soludo as a governor with vision and conviction, Shettima said the projects being commissioned in the state reflected efforts to address the needs of residents and stimulate economic activities. He further said the Tinubu administration was treating all regions fairly, insisting that the South-East was a priority under the Renewed Hope Agenda. In his remarks, Soludo thanked residents of Ekwulobia for their patience during the construction of the flyover, acknowledging the inconveniences caused by the project, including the demolition of several buildings. He said the flyover and the Solution Market were part of efforts to address traffic congestion and improve urban planning in the area. “Ekwulobia has evolved from chaos to a sprawling city and it is the capital of Old Aguata Union. The site of this flyover used to be a motor park and was blocking the road, with roadside traders turning it into a chaotic scene. The Solution Market was also built to decongest the area. I want to say that a new city, Ekwulobia, is born,” the governor said. He said the administration’s vision of making Anambra a liveable and prosperous state required deliberate investment in town planning and urban regeneration. Soludo added that construction work on other new cities across the state was progressing, expressing optimism that several completed projects would be ready for commissioning after the January 2027 governorship election. The 300-metre Ekwulobia flyover, which was completed about a year ago, has its adjoining roads already open to motorists. The post Tinubu approves free trade zone, two flyovers for Anambra appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ces sept Sénégalais dans le Top 100 du Choiseul Africa
items.description: Choiseul a publié son classement des figures économiques les plus influentes. Sept sénégalais figurent parmi les nominés. A la découverte de ces figures qui font bouger les lignes. Marie-Reine Tekou-Asubonteng, figure féminine du secteur minier Parmi les décideurs économiques figurant au prestigieux palmarès Choiseul 100 Africa 2026, Marie-Reine Tekou-Asubonteng se singularise par un parcours à la croisée de la finance, de la gouvernance et de la stratégie industrielle. Ce classement met en lumière les dirigeants africains de 40 ans et moins qui contribuent au dynamisme économique du continent. Directrice générale de Makabingui Gold Operation et Country Director de Bishop Resources au Sénégal, elle est la première femme à diriger une mine industrielle au Sénégal. Son parcours, nourri par une formation en finance d’entreprise à HEC Paris et en leadership à la Harvard Kennedy School, associe expertise financière, maîtrise des enjeux de gouvernance et capacité à conduire des transformations organisationnelles complexes. À la tête de Makabingui Gold Operation depuis 2024, elle pilote la réorganisation structurelle et stratégique de l’entreprise, avec pour priorités la consolidation de son cadre institutionnel, la modernisation de ses mécanismes de gestion et la préparation industrielle du projet. La particularité de son mandat réside dans la conduite simultanée de deux chantiers étroitement liés : la transformation de l’organisation et le développement de son actif industriel. Une démarche qui exige une maîtrise des arbitrages financiers, une hiérarchisation rigoureuse des investissements et une capacité à inscrire les décisions opérationnelles dans une stratégie de long terme. Dans une industrie fortement capitalistique, la création de valeur se construit bien avant les premières onces produites. Elle repose autant sur la pertinence des choix d’investissement que sur la capacité de l’entreprise à mobiliser ses ressources, à structurer ses équipes et à transformer ses orientations stratégiques en réalisations concrètes. Jouldée Soumaré, une voix du secteur privé Au Sénégal, Jouldée Soumaré a eu à occuper le poste de Directrice du Développement du Secteur Privé (DDSP) au sein du Ministère de l'Économie, du Plan et de la Coopération du Sénégal. Avant d'intégrer l'administration publique en 2024, elle a exercé pendant plus de douze ans dans le secteur bancaire. De 2021 à 2024, elle a été Directrice Générale Adjointe de Bank Espace Pro à Société Générale. Avant cela, entre 2016 et 2021, elle a été Chargée d'affaires professionnels puis directrice d'agence. Auparavant, de 2013 à 2016, elle a été conseillère clientèle privéé à Groupe Crédit du Nord Au plan académique, Jouldee Soumare est titulaire d'un Master en banque, finance, monnaie et marché de l'Université Paris Nanterre, d'un Master en activités bancaires (IAE France), d'une licence du CNAM et d’un DUT technique de commercialisation de l'Université de Bourgogne. Elle fait partie des LEAD Fellows distingués par The Africa CEO Forum pour son engagement dans la transformation du service public africain et l'appui à l'entrepreneuriat Fatoumata Ba, une experte de la finance Fatoumata BA est Investisseur en Capital Risque, Fondatrice & Présidente de Janngo et Associée Gérante de Janngo Capital. Janngo finance et développe des champions digitaux panafricains combinant performance économique et impact social positif. Avant cela, elle a été Fondatrice et PDG de Jumia en Côte d’Ivoire, Directrice générale de Jumia au Nigeria et Membre du Comité Exécutif Afrique. Elle a notamment été distinguée en qualité de ‘Young Global Leader’ du Forum Économique Mondial. La boite qu’elle dirige, à pour vocation de financer, créer et accompagner des start-ups africaines orientées vers la « technologie pour le bien », alliant performance économique et impact social inclusif, avec un accent fort sur les entreprises dirigées par des femmes ou destinées aux femmes. Aida Diouf, l’engagement social Parmi le top 100 de Choiseul, Aida Diouf est directrice exécutive de Camusat depuis janvier 2024. Ellen a rejoint ledit Groupe Camusat en 2018 en tant que Responsable Administrative et Financière pour l'Afrique et l'Océan Indien, où elle avait en charge 17 pays. Au plan académique, Aïda Diouf est diplômée de Toulouse Business School avec une spécialisation en Audit et Finance d'Entreprise. Elle a complété sa formation avec un Master en comptabilité avancée et également en gestion des entreprises. S’agissant de sa carrière professionnelle, elle a fait ses débuts chez Mazars à Paris en tant qu'auditrice. Par la suite, elle a évolué en tant que contrôleuse financière des entités internationales au sein de BNP Personal Finance où elle a eu l'opportunité de développer et de renforcer son expertise financière. Elhadji Mamadou Seck, Directeur général de Sococim Industries Primé dans le Top 100 du Choiseul, Elhadji Mamadou Seck est le Directeur général de SOCOCIM Industries, filiale sénégalaise du groupe cimentier Vicat basée à Rufisque. Il occupe ce poste depuis mai 2023, succédant à Youga Sow devenu président du conseil d'administration. Avant cette promotion, il a eu à occuper le poste Directeur général au Mali (2018–2023) et contrôleur de gestion en Afrique de l'Ouest (2014–2018) pour le groupe Vicat. Elhadji Mamadou Seck a débuté sa carrière en tant que Contrôleur financier chez ArcelorMittal (2010–2014) et comptable consolidation chez AREVA (2009–2010) en France. Au plan académique, il est Diplômé d'ISC Paris (2010) et d'ESSEC Executive Education. Khady Evelyne Denise Ndiaye, un engagement pour le développement régional Khady Evelyne Denis Ndiaye occupe le poste de Directrice du Secteur Privé depuis janvier 2019, où elle pilote l'amélioration du climat des affaires et l'émergence de champions économiques régionaux. Elle a démarré sa carrière comme chargée de mission veille et intelligence économique auprès de l'Agence régionale pour le développement économique du Limousin. Khady Evelyn Denise Ndiaye a intègré la Commission de l'UEMOA en 2010, occupant des postes en intelligence stratégique avant de devenir Cheffe de la Division de l'amélioration du climat des affaires en 2016. Elle est titulaire d’un Master 2 en Intelligence économique (Université Toulouse 1 Capitole) et un Master 2 en Développement et financement du secteur privé (CERDI – Université d'Auvergne en partenariat avec le CEFEB de l'AFD). Khady Evelyn Denise Ndiaye est également dans l’entreprenariat à travers son label « Maison KED » Marieme Sav Sow, une étoile du management Marième-Sav SOW est Vice-Présidente Engagement & Advocacy (Engagement et Plaidoyer) pour l'Afrique chez TotalEnergies, basée au siège parisien depuis septembre 2025, et présidente de la Fondation MAM. Elle a rejoint l'entreprise en 2010 et y a occupé différents postes dans plusieurs zones géographiques. Elle a notamment été Managing Director and Country Chair / Directrice générale de TotalEnergies Marketing Madagasikara à partir de 2022, après des expériences chez Argedis en France (2017–2019) et en Tanzanie (2019–2022). Par la suite, elle a été promue au poste de Vice-Présidente Engagement & Advocacy au sein de la branche Exploration & Production Afrique en septembre 2025. Avant l’expérience Total Energie, Marième Sav Sow a travaillé dans la finance en banque d'investissement, notamment comme Senior Reporting & Compliance Specialist chez State Street à Boston, puis comme Financial Manager aux États-Unis et au Cameroun.
